articleTitle: Transfer Learning based High-Speed Link Transient Modeling Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Accurate and effective signal integrity modeling methods play a crucial role in the iterative process of highspeed link design. Data-driven deep learning demonstrates reliable time-domain transient modeling capabilities; however, it frequently overlooks associations between links with similar structures, necessitating retraining for each specific case. This paper introduces a transfer learning-based deep gated recurrent unit (TL-DGRU) network for high-speed link transient modeling. The approach enhances the generalization of deep learning methods by transferring knowledge from a pre-trained model to the current task and fine-tuning it. Experimental results in high-speed link applications demonstrate that the TL-DGRU method significantly improves eye diagram prediction performance through transfer learning, achieving a $53.8 \%$ reduction in normalized mean square error and a $31.4 \%$ reduction in normalized mean absolute error: This study validates the effectiveness of transfer learning in enhancing the generalization and adaptability of transient simulation models for high-speed links across various scenarios.

articleTitle: EMC of Linear and Non-Linear Loads in Different EM Environments; An Issue of Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Renewable energy sources (RES) are being widely implemented in electricity systems to decarbonize energy supplies, including those in the most remote areas. In the context of the rural electrification effort in Indonesia, the impact of several common household appliances on grid voltages was determined. Modifications to the supply impedance have emulated the contextual issues that were discussed in previous literature, like extremely long distribution cables or ad-hoc modifications of the RES. The voltage rms fluctuation and voltage total harmonic distortion were examined. The results show that voltage deviation, noise, and harmonic were highly affected in the case of nonlinear loads. In the case of linear loads, as expected, the voltage quality will depend on the supply. Therefore, understanding the source impedance characteristics can be used to help maintain the EMC while using power-efficient nonlinear loads.

articleTitle: Reference Measurement for Inter-Laboratory Comparison of Electric Field Uniformity for Radiated Immunity Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Since the differences of the electric field uniformity among the laboratories degrade reliability in the quality of radiated immunity tests, they must be investigated and improved. However, the reference value of the electric field uniformity measurement differs depending on the laboratories. To evaluate the sources of the differences of the electric field uniformity, a reliable standard must be established, and deviations from the standard are evaluated. In this study, the reference uniformity corresponding to the radiation pattern of the antenna in free space was obtained. In addition, the inter-laboratory comparison of the electric field uniformity was carried out, and the characteristic of each anechoic chamber by the deviation from the reference value was evaluated.

articleTitle: DUT Response to Radiated Electromagnetic Fields in a Continuously Stirred Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Reverberation chambers enable robust measurements of immunity to radiated electromagnetic fields. The modestirred operating mode, in which the boundary conditions are continuously changed, is particularly time-efficient. However, problems can arise if the devices under test (DUT) do not respond quickly enough to the field variation, so that interference effects caused by the external field remain falsely undetected. This work deals with how the speed of the field change can be quantitatively adapted to the response time of devices under test. For this purpose, an artificial DUT was developed, with which a realistic test object with certain temporal response characteristics can be imitated. Measurements were performed to determine how the stirring speed can affect the temporal characteristics of the power injected into the DUT and its response.

articleTitle: “13 Reasons Why”: Rationale and Preliminary Statistical Approach for Classifying Electromagnetic Disturbances in Healthcare Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Modern healthcare environments are complex and diverse with respect to electromagnetic disturbances (EMD). The amount of electrical equipment and equipment integration used during medical procedures poses intrinsic risks for patients. This paper briefs the rationale for classifying EMD sources and environments by using statistical models applied to electromagnetic field data measured in a real hospital in the Netherlands aiming to develop a model for the quantification of the electromagnetic interference risks. The preliminary results indicate the potential of applying statistical analysis models and methods for electromagnetic environment classification purposes.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies of High Frequency Performances of Plated Through Hole and Coaxial Via in Printed Circuit Boards Up to 110 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper shows the high frequency transmission performances experimentally for plated through hole (PTH) and coaxial via (CV) in printed circuit boards (PCBs) up to 110 GHz, by using double-sided probing techniques of scattering parameter (S-parameter) measurements. The short-open-load-reciprocal (SOLR) calibration is done to set the measured reference planes to the probe tips with aids of a commercial impedance standard substrate (ISS) in short/open/load standards and the CV as the reciprocal standard. The measured results indicate the PTH has transmission performance similar to a planar transmission line below 72 GHz while the CV can extend to 85 GHz with some little ripples due to impedance mismatch in this specific study case.

articleTitle: Research and Analysis of Electromagnetic Compatibility Radiated Emission Testing Methods for Automotive Dynamic Driving Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper introduces an electromagnetic compatibility radiation emission testing method based on dynamic driving condition We conducted dynamic condition tests on both pure electric vehicles and fuel-powered vehicles using our existing experimental setup. Based on the test results obtained from actual vehicles, the necessity and significance of dynamic condition testing are discussed.

articleTitle: Mode Impedance Measurement of Black Box System Using Two Probe Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper introduces the black box modeling of the motor driving system in electric vehicles. The proposed black box model includes both differential mode impedance and common mode impedance for each source. Accurate measurement of these impedances is crucial for predicting conducted emissions using simulation. In this study, mode impedance is measured while the switching module is in a working state, employing an inductive coupling probe. As impedances vary over time during the working state, we consider the maximum and minimum ranges of differential mode impedance. Unlike the differential mode, the common mode impedance remains almost constant when the switching module is operational.

articleTitle: Field-and-Circuit Co-Analysis of Mode Conversion Caused by Continuous Imbalance Factor Changes in Three-Conductor System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The direct connection of a microstrip line (MSL) to a parallel-line cable causes mode conversion that is proportional to the difference in the imbalance factor of the transmission lines, which can be represented by the modalequivalent-circuit model. In this paper, we first demonstrate that mode conversion occurs where the distance between the parallel-line cable and the system ground changes continuously in the immunity evaluation system. The mode conversion occurs when the parallel-line cable is placed perpendicular to the system ground, whereas no mode conversion occurs when the parallel-line cable is placed parallel to the system ground. Next, we clarify that the mode conversion can be represented by using a staircase approximation to represent the continuously changing imbalance factor as the distance between the parallelline cable and the system ground changes. It was found that the differential-mode (DM) voltage caused by mode conversion was successfully analyzed using the modal equivalent-circuit model that utilizes field and circuit co-analysis in the commercial simulator HFSS. Furthermore, it was found that increasing the number of steps in the staircase approximation approaches the spectrum obtained in the full-wave calculations.

articleTitle: Statistical Eye Diagram for Nonideal Decision Feedback Equalizer (DFE)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper introduces the statistical eye diagram for the nonideal decision feedback equalizer (DFE). The DFE equalizes the inter-symbol-interference (ISI) based on the previous bits the DFE makes decisions. However, a DFE may make a wrong bit decision due to a substantial amount of noise, which is defined as a nonideal DFE in this paper. The statistical eye diagram was proposed for efficient signal integrity (SI) analysis, however, it is not applicable to the nonideal DFE. Because the statistical eye diagram has variables of the sampled voltage and sampling time. The DFE includes variables of a threshold voltage and sampling time for a slicer, which leads to a dependency between the variables and the corresponding statistical eye diagram. Thus, this paper proposes the statistical eye diagram for the nonideal DFE. The proposed method is verified by comparison to the transient simulation.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of EMP Simulator Using Different Simulation Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper aims to compare an experimental and a simulated design of an Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) generator. It focuses on numerical simulations carried out through Computer Simulation Technology (CST) studio compared to an experiment. The aim is to analyze the impact of different configurations in the simulated environment that satisfy the pulse criteria and simulation complexity. Different types of boundaries are considered to observe the effects on the simulated pulse waveforms. Since the numerical simulation utilizes a perfect double exponential waveform for an ideal scenario (reference), a correction factor is later introduced based on the measured Electric field (E-field). The correction factor is calculated using the transfer functions from simulations to get a corrected E-field at the center of the test volume. Other E-field sensors are used to analyze the accuracy of the corrected simulation.

articleTitle: Fundamental Study on Electromagnetic Analysis Attack Detection using Oscillation Shift of Ring Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electromagnetic analysis attacks that extract secret data from a cryptographic IC by measuring and analyzing changes in electromagnetic (EM) fields have been reported. Against such attacks, it is effective to detect an EM field probe in the measurement stage, which is the preliminary stage of the analysis. A detection method using magnetic field coupling between the sensor coil, which makes up an LC oscillator in the chip and an EM probe has been proposed. However, their detection distance is limited to the inside of the chip, and EM field measurement from outside the chip is not covered by this method. In this paper, we propose a detection method using the capacitance change of a metallic film formed above the chip, which is capacitively coupled to the EM probe. The metallic film, applied externally to cover the entire IC, has the capability to detect an EM probe over a wide range, independent of the EM probe’s orientation. To achieve high-precision detection, a ring oscillator is configured with the metallic film as part of the wiring and its frequency change is used. As a result, we confirm that an EM probe is detectable at distances of up to 6 mm directly above the chip.

articleTitle: Impact of Dead Time Effect on Common Mode Electromagnetic Interference in PMSM Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The pulse width modulation (PWM) technique has been widely applied in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives, which causes common mode (CM) electromagnetic interference (EMI) issue due to its higher frequency. And moreover, this issue will be intensified by the dead time area inserted into the control signal of the switching device (such as IGBT or MOSFET) in the power inverter. In this paper, the CM voltage/current has been analyzed with the considerations of the switching process of the MOSFET as well as the influence of the dead time effect. In order to reduce the CM voltage/current, a dead time compensation method is recommended, which can reduce the distortion of CM voltage/current and relieve the high-frequency (HF) CM EMI noise. According to experiment result, it can be figured out that the spectra of the CM current have been reduced by nearly 5.5 dB $\mu$A at the resonance frequency with an appropriate dead time compensation in PMSM drives.

articleTitle: Radiation Characteristics of TEM Horn and Broadband Sleeve Antennas Used for Near-Field Radiated Immunity Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The field radiation characteristics in the vicinity of a TEM horn and a broadband sleeve were evaluated experimentally. Both antennas are used in the near-field radiated immunity test, however, their different radiation characteristics affect the test results. The electric field distribution and propagation characteristics of each antenna show the differences in the electric field applied inside the EUT.

Author Keywords: radiated immunity test in close proximity

articleTitle: Circuit Model Construction for Simulating ESD Discharge Current Flowing through CMCs and ESD Suppression Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electrostatic discharge (ESD) damage evaluation methods for common mode choke (CMC) and ESD suppression devices are standardized as IEC 62228-5 Annex E and Annex F, respectively. In this test, it is not possible to measure the current waveform flowing into the input section of the electronic device. Against this background, in this study, we investigated an equivalent circuit model that allows to know the discharge current waveform flowing into and through the CMC and ESD suppression device under test in advance using SPICE without performing measurements. Specifically, we examined the equivalent circuit model of the ESD gun and test board used in LTspice, and verified their validity by checking whether the voltage waveforms at the output of the test boards match the actual measurements. As a result, the model is valid to estimate the 1 st peak level and rise time of the discharge currents flowing through a CMC and the entire discharge current flowing through an ESD suppression device, within an error range of approximately $30 \%$.

articleTitle: Application of the Three-Dimentional FDTD method to the Analysis of Lightning-Induced Surges in Secondary Circuits of a Substation owing to a Lightning Impulse Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In case of a direct lightning strike to a substation and transmission line, some parts of the lightning current flow into the grounding structure of the substation, and they may induce overvoltages in the secondary circuit of the substation owing to the effect of the transient ground potential rises of the grounding structure and electromagnetic coupling. In this study, we applied the three-dimensional flnite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, which is one of the numerical electromagnetic computation methods, to the analysis of the transient response of grounding grids and surges induced on the shielded control cable of a test platform of the primary and secondary circuits of a substation, and confirmed the applicability of the FDTD method by comparing the simulated results with measured waveforms.

articleTitle: Influence of Electrode Surface Roughness on Radiated Electromagnetic Field Strength due to Micro-Gap ESD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In order to investigate the electromagnetic noise characteristics caused by micro-gap ESD, influence of electrode surface roughness on radiated electromagnetic field strength was examined. The roughness of the electrode surface was varied from about 1 μm to 13 μm using the emulsion compound and lapping film abrasives. As a result, the radiated electric field strength varied depending on the roughness of the electrode surface, and the radiated field strength was highest at the electrode with the least roughness of 1 μm. Moreover, no difference in electric field strength was observed for roughness of about 3 μm or more.

articleTitle: Malfunction of a Wearable Device Caused by Potential Drop of a Charged Proximity Object due to Electrostatic Discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In the actual situations of wearable devices used, there is a situation where a human body and devices that a human holds are charged to high voltage, and their potential rapidly drops when electrostatic discharge (ESD) from the human body to a surrounding object occurs. In this situation, our previous studies observed that a long-duration induced noise with exponential decay in the order of tens to hundreds of microseconds under the condition that the input circuit of the device had high impedance. The noise could cause wearable devices malfunction due to its long duration. In this study, we examined whether malfunctions occur in a wearable device in the floating state near the charged object when the potential of the charged object drops rapidly due to ESD. We also considered the cause of the malfunctions from the perspective of both the long-duration induced noise and the indirect ESD. From experimental results, we confirmed that malfunctions occur in the wearable device in the floating state near the charged object when the potential of the charged object drops rapidly due to ESD. Additional experimental results showed that the main cause of the malfunctions is the long-duration induced noise.

articleTitle: Underdefined Power Quality in Rural DC Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: DC energy systems are gaining popularity and are expected to experience a growing complexity. Especially in the context of energy access, where energy poor communities get connected to modern means of electricity and clean cooking, reliability of the energy systems is of paramount importance. Power quality for dc energy systems is however underdefined and could very well turn out to be an obstacle for energy access if left unattended. This paper analyzes how poor dc power quality could adversely influence the lifetime of energy systems and shows examples of these mechanisms through measurements on ten different off-the-shelf dc powersources.

articleTitle: Cost-Efficient Snubbers for Boost Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Conventional boost converters operating with hard-switching result in low conversion efficiency and increased electromagnetic interference emissions. In this paper, a cost-efficient passive snubber is proposed with a few additional components: two diodes, one capacitor, and one inductor. Moreover, because these snubber components are not located on the main power processing path, they only require low ratings, resulting in improved cost-effectiveness.

articleTitle: Accurate Extraction for Inductance of Position Indicator Coil in Noisy Environment Using DC Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper deals with a method to accurately measure the inductance of the position indicator (PI) coil in a noisy environment. It was verified that the proposed method can form the constant permeability distribution over time by flowing DC current to an additional coil below the PI coil through simulation. It was confirmed that the inductance of PI coil varies linearly depending on the position of the control rod. In addition, the relationship between the position of the control rod and inductance was derived. Using the relationship, the position of the control rod can be estimated from the inductance with an error within $7 \%$.

articleTitle: The Estimation of Cable Input Impedance Through Analytical Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, two analytical techniques for computing the input impedance of cables are introduced. Given the pivotal role of the SMA connector in altering cable input impedance, it is essential to account for the significant effect of the connector in the impedance calculations. This effect is addressed through the use of two models for the connector, namely the circuit model and the cascade model. These analytical techniques can be applied to various cables, provided that the impedance of the cable up to the connector is known, and the impact of the connector on the input impedance is appropriately considered by the models.

articleTitle: A Study on Reverberation Chamber using Parallel-plate TEM Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: ISO11451-5 was published in May 2023 as a vehicle immunity test standard limited to reverberation chambers. In this study, we have designed a new parallel-plate Transverse Electromagnetic (TEM) antenna compliant with Transmission Line System (TLS) described in Annex E as an immunity test method from 10 kHz to Lowest Useable Frequency (LUF), fabricated a $1 / 4$ scale reverberation chamber, evaluated electric field uniformity, and ascertained its effectiveness. Further, using a $1 / 4$ vehicle scale model, we have compared this immunity test method using a new parallel-plate TEM antenna with the conventional immunity test methods using a TLS and a biconical antenna at Absorber Lined Shielded Enclosure (ALSE) to ascertain its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Explanation of Convolutional Neural Network for Automotive Wire Harness Using Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper describes a methodology for explaining a convolutional neural network (CNN) for automotive wire harness using a gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM). Previous studies have achieved the judgement of the automotive wire harness using a machine learning (ML) technique. However, due to the black-box nature of ML-based methods, there is a lack of transparency, leading to a lack of trust in experimental results and hindering further research progress. In this paper, we propose how to obtain an activation map by applying Grad-CAM to explain the CNN model and get a more intuitive understanding of the mechanism behind harness diagnosis.

articleTitle: Tolerance Evaluation Against Deep Learning Side-Channel Attack on AES in Automotive Microcontroller With Uncertain Leakage Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Side-channel attacks (SCAs) pose a threat to cryptographic security because they potentially recover cryptographic secret-keys by analyzing electromagnetic noise from cryptographic ICs. Interest in automotive security has been growing in recent years, resulting in a demand for SCA tolerance evaluation of automotive ICs. In the current paper, we implemented AES128 in software on the Renesas RH850 series microcontroller and demonstrated leading SCA methods such as correlation power analysis (CPA) and deep learning SCA (DL-SCA). CPA needs leakage models and is therefore more powerful against unprotected AES in the ATmega series and the STM series. However, our results show that CPA fails to recover all bytes of the cryptographic secret-key even with 800,000 leakage traces, whereas DL-SCA succeeds in recovering all bytes of the key. These results differ from those with ATmega and STM series, indicating that information leakage from the microcontroller is sufficient to recover the keys, but that the conventional leakage model is not valid for CPA.

articleTitle: A Novel Intelligent Antenna Synthesis Method Based on Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel intelligent method for antenna synthesis utilizing a Deep Neural Network (DNN) model. The proposed method can provide appropriate geometric parameters according to the input performance requirements of the antenna, such as bandwidth, resonant frequency and specific absorption rate (SAR). To verify the accuracy and effectiveness of this method, an inverted-F antenna applied in the mobile phone is used as an example. The mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of geometric parameter prediction is 3.511%. In addition, the results are compared with the traditional data-driven model and the ensemble learning model. This method can be widely applied in practical antenna design.

articleTitle: Surge Characteristics Induced in the Secondary Circuits by a Lightning Impulse Current Injected into the Grounding Grid: An Experimental Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In substations, the failure of secondary circuits due to lightning surges is a significant concern with respect to surge disturbances. When a lightning surge enters a substation from the transmission-line side, it is divided between the primary circuits and the grounding grid through the action of lightning arresters. This division may result in varying trends in the induced surge characteristics within the secondary circuits, influenced by the distinct paths and the sensitivity to certain geometric parameters of the primary/secondary circuits. Consequently, characterizing them individually is crucial. Using a test platform for the primary/secondary circuits of gasinsulated substations, this study conducts an experimental study on the surge characteristics induced in vulnerable circuits when a lightning impulse current is injected into the grounding structure. An emphasis is placed on the effects of cable length and its position on the induced surge characteristics by utilizing the routes of a control cable as a parameter.

articleTitle: Investigation of Mode Transformation in Motor Control System of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Exposed to Intentional Electromagnetic Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Susceptibility acts as a critical metric for assessing an electrical apparatus’s performance and reliability amidst the external electromagnetic environment, especially the intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI). Given that the IEMI often invades electrical systems in common-mode (CM) and converts to the differential-mode (DM) signal to disrupt the normal operation of devices, investigating the mode transformation in the system under attack is pivotal for its susceptibility analysis. This paper first investigates the CM to DM conversion in the motor control system of the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) illuminated by an external IEMI. Experimental studies explore the influence of the distance between UAV and copper ground on mode conversion, revealing that adjusting the UAV’s landing gear height have the potential to enhance its susceptibility.

articleTitle: Worst-Scenario Prediction for Field-to-Cable Coupling Under Continuous Intentional Electromagnetic Interference Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Studying intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI) is crucial for safeguarding hardware safety, as it helps to address the deliberate disruption of electronic devices. The field-to-cable coupling serves as a prevalent attack mechanism of IEMI, precipitating unexpected failures of the device under test. Many efforts focus on the analysis of field-to-cable coupling under high-power electromagnetic pulse, but less target on the phenomenon illuminated with continuous waves. This paper proposes a novel method to predict the worst-case for field-tocable coupling under continuous IEMI attack. By employing the transmission line theory to characterize the cables and obtaining the impedance information of the devices at both ends of the cable, an analytical model is built for determining the terminal voltage frequency responses induced by IEMI. Subsequently, the sensitive frequency region of this cable-connected electrical system can be determined, facilitating purposive immunity improvements. Using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) as an example, the analytical calculations are compared with the radiated susceptibility test. The results exhibit a good agreement with experiments and validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Time and Frequency Domains Evaluation of Crosstalk on Differential Lines with Meander Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The meander structures in printed circuit boards (PCBs) are designed to compensate for signal skew in differential transmission lines. They introduce heterogeneous impedance, raising concerns about signal integrity. Despite the known issues, the impact of meander structures in differential lines, particularly their influence on adjacent lines, has not been investigated. In this study, we analyze the effects of meander structures on both near-end Crosstalk (NEXT) and far-end Crosstalk (FEXT) through 8-port mixed-mode S-parameters and step pulse analysis, using finite-difference time-domain simulations. Our findings indicate that in NEXT assessments, voltage fluctuations are primarily attributable to reflections from the meander structure. In contrast, FEXT is mitigated as the meander structure prolongs the rise time of signals propagating through the aggressor line.

articleTitle: Passive Cancellation Method for Common-Mode Noise Based on a Nonlinear Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: AC-DC converters almost always require common-mode (CM) filters to restrict conducting their electromagnetic interference (EMI) emissions to the power grid and ensure compliance with EMI certification requirements. These CM filters, which are based on the well-known LC lowpass filter, are typically bulky and expensive. Hence, a method for passive $\mathbf{C M}$ current cancellation using a nonlinear model is proposed herein. This method is entirely composed of passive components and offers advantages in terms of cost and system reliability. Compared to conventional passive LC filters, the number of magnetic components remains unchanged. This study proposes the derivation of a nonlinear model to estimate the filter performance using measured data from an actual CM choke; however, the proposed method does not require the mathematical model of a CM choke.

articleTitle: Characteristics of a Long Duration Noise Induced on a Wearable Devices by Potential Drop of a Charged Proximity Object Caused by ESD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In an actual situation where wearable devices are used, there is a situation where the device is charged along with a human body to high voltage, and their potential rapidly drops when electrostatic discharge (ESD) from the human body to a surrounding object occurs. In this situation, our previous studies observed that a long-duration induced noise with exponential decay in the order of tens to hundreds of microseconds under the condition that the input circuit of the device had high impedance. In this study, we measured the fundamental characteristics of the long-duration induced noise by varying conditions, such as that with/without a case of the circuit, the case’s material, and the circuit’s structure, using a simple verification circuit consisting of only an $R C$ circuit and plates. As a result, we found that a long-duration induced noise with a large amplitude is induced when the electric field from the charging plate couples imbalance to the GND or HOT side of the circuit. It was also found that the amplitude of the long-duration induced noise became smaller due to the cancellation of the electrostatic induction when the electrical field couples to both the GND and HOT sides. These results support our hypothesis of the inducing mechanism of the long-duration noise.

articleTitle: AI Workbench - Conceptual Workflow to Develop AI Models for SI/PI-Applications in PCB Development
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper presents an initial concept for a so-called AI Workbench. It is based on corresponding preliminary work and experience from the EMC Workbench and the development of $\mathrm{AI} / \mathrm{ML}$ models for $\mathrm{SI} / \mathrm{PI}$ design problems. After introducing a process for reducing SI/PI analysis complexity in PCB design through the use of $\mathrm{AI} / \mathrm{ML}$ models, an introduction to the development of $A I / M L$ models for the prediction of SI/PI design solutions is given using two selected examples on the subject of SI and PI. Based on these considerations, a workflow for the development of $A I$ models for SI/PI applications in PCB development is presented. The presented concept takes into account the work steps that must be taken into account when developing $\mathrm{AI} / \mathrm{ML}$ models for $\mathrm{SI} / \mathrm{PI}$ applications. These results are then incorporated into an approach for the development of a workbench to support the systematic generation of $\mathrm{AI} / \mathrm{ML}$ models for the $\mathrm{SI} / \mathrm{PI}$ area.

articleTitle: Application of the Model From CISPR 16-4-4 for the Derivation of Limits for Power Drive Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electrical equipment needs to meet disturbance limits to ensure the protection of radio services. In most cases, generic limits are applied which are related to the type of location where equipment is intended to be used. However, in some cases those limits are deemed not to be appropriate, partly because of economic boundary conditions associated with measures to mitigate disturbances, partly because they are used at locations or under conditions with a lower risk of interfering with radio services. Hence, modified limits might be a choice to consider the constraints of equipment on one hand, and nevertheless to reduce the minimum of interference to radio services on the other hand. A procedure how to derive such modified limits is given in the document CISPR TR 16-4-4 in which a probabilistic approach is used. This paper describes these aspects of the approach which are relevant for a particular category of power drive systems and proposes some probability factors which can be used as input for the deriving of radiated disturbance limits in the frequency range from 30 MHz to 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of Crosstalk Between a Microstrip Line and Two Ground Slots Placed Both Sides
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: By advance of miniaturization of electronic devices, grounds of a printed circuit board (PCB) are tend to be small and complicated and may have some defects, such as connectors or clearance halls of vias. In this paper, we analyzed the crosstalk (electromagnetic coupling) between a microstrip line and two ground slot placed on the both sides of it on a PCB using the multi-conductor transmission lines method to estimate the voltages on the ground slot. To calculate by using the MTL method, per-unit-length parameters, such as the self and mutual capacitances and inductances of a microstrip line and a ground slot were calculated using the spectral domain approach. We calculated the coupling voltages in the ground slot excited by the microstrip line using the MTL method and the FDTD method and showed the validity of the proposed method by comparing the results of both methods when the microstrip line and the two ground slots were located closely. Finally, we calculated the coupling voltages in the ground slots versus the edge to edge distance between a microstrip line and ground slot and showed that the accuracy of the MTL method within the frequency which is lower than several GHz.

articleTitle: Application of the Impedance Balance Method to Electric Compressor System with an Integrated Mechanical and Electrical Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The impedance balance method is used as a countermeasure against electromagnetic noise in power electronic circuits. In a previous research, the authors’ research group confirmed the reduction of common-mode voltage in a three-phase inverter circuit using the impedance balance method. However, it has been difficult to reduce common-mode voltage using conventional methods in an electric compressor system with an integrated mechanical and electrical structure, where the three-phase inverter and motor are housed in a single housing. This research describes a method to reduce the common-mode voltage in an electric compressor system with an integrated mechanical and electrical structure, using an impedance balance method. The first is to reduce the impedance of the balancing elements added to the circuit, and the second is to increase the impedance of the three three-phase output line connecting the three-phase inverter and the motor. By combining these two methods, the frequency bandwidth of the reduction effect was expanded from 2 MHz to 30 MHz, and a reduction in common-mode voltage of up to 30 dB was confirmed.

articleTitle: Morris Sensitivity Analysis on Conducted Emissions of an Inverting Buck–Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility simulations of switched-mode power supplies are essential, as fast switching of high power can result in unacceptable electromagnetic emissions. This paper presents an easy-to-use methodology to highlight the major contributors to increased conducted emissions due to parallel RLC resonant circuits. The Morris method for global sensitivity analysis is applied to the frequency response of a DC-DC converter. This allows rapid detection of electronic components responsible for emissions in a specific frequency range. A link to Sobol’s total sensitivity index is proposed to determine the relative contribution of each component. Thus, contributors to electromagnetic interference can be quickly identified and weighted, enabling improved root cause analysis.

articleTitle: Design Methodology of Through-Silicon via for Crosstalk Optimization Based on Impedance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, we propose the optimal crosstalk condition for through-silicon via (TSV) based on the impedance. We propose and analyze an optimal TSV design methodology based solely on the impedance of TSVs, rather than relying on shielding structures and crosstalk cancellation on-chip schemes. Furthermore, we analyze TSV crosstalk in different situations by defining scenarios based on the presence or absence of loading termination.

articleTitle: Investigation of Wideband Spline-Based Spearhead-Shaped Printed Antenna for EMC Radiated Emission Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility of a spline-based spearhead-shaped printed antenna (SSPA) for EMC radiated emission testing. The SSPA is designed to have a wideband frequency response with the main bandwidth from around the frequency of 1.6 GHz to more than 20 GHz with a notch band at around the frequency of 1.9 GHz to 3.47 GHz. The investigation is carried out by comparing the performance of SSPA with the standard Ultralog antenna used in electromagnetic compatibility (EMC)/electromagnetic interference (EMI) testing. Three frequency bands are emitted from the signal sources, i.e., Wi-Fi access points and signal generators, which produce emissions at the frequency bands of 2.4 GHz, 4 GHz, and 5.8 GHz. As the reference, the Ultralog antenna is capable of detecting emissions in those three bands at the signal levels of $111.14 \mathrm{~dB} \mu \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}, 88.60 \mathrm{~dB} \mu \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}$, and 110.87 $\mathrm{dB} \mu \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}$, respectively. Meanwhile, the SSPA can also detect well the emission at the frequencies of 2.4GHz and 4GHz bands with the levels of $102.51 \mathrm{~dB} \mu \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}$ and $84.57 \mathrm{~dB} \mu \mathrm{V} / \mathrm{m}$, respectively. In general, the SSPA has good prospects for further development by considering several recommendations.

articleTitle: Measured Traces Reduction Using SNR of Leakage for Tolerance Evaluation to Deep Learning-based Side-channel Attack
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Side-channel Attacks (SCAs) are threats to decrypt cryptography by analyzing the switching noise from cryptographic ICs. Additionally, Deep Learning-based SCAs (DLSCAs) can break masking-protected cryptography, a popular countermeasure to conventional SCAs. Hence, it is required to evaluate tolerance to DL-SCAs for possible countermeasures. In this paper, we propose a method to reduce the number of leakage trace measurements for evaluation. In the proposed method, we first measure the leakage traces when a SNR of leakage is high and low. Next, we add Gaussian noise on a high SNR traces to make its SNR equal to a low SNR. This method applies correlation power analysis (CPA) to identify a low SNR, and it requires a smaller number of traces than when running an actual attack. Therefore, this method enables the reduction of measured traces. We measured leakage traces of a microcontroller implementing the masking-protected AES-128. As the results, this method predicts that 9 out of 12 secret key bytes are recovered, and this is almost consistent with the measured one.

articleTitle: Challenges in Feasible Simulation of Side-Channel Attack Resistance for Cryptographic Hardware
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Cryptographic hardware plays a crucial role in establishing the Root of Trust to ensure information security in various applications, including IoT devices, autonomous driving systems, and digital ecosystems. Critical Security Parameters (CSPs) like cryptographic engines and keys must be securely stored within a hardware-protected cryptographic boundary to enhance security. This paper comprehensively reviews methods for evaluating resistance against Side-Channel Attacks (SCA). It introduces research that employs the signal-to-noise ratio of Side-Channel (SC) leakage. The objective is to facilitate an efficient evaluation of SCA resistance for the development of practical designs of cryptographic hardware.

articleTitle: Innovative 4-Terminal Capacitor: A Versatile Solution for Enhanced EMC/SI Performance and Layout Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel 4-terminal capacitor design, presenting a comprehensive exploration of its structure, applications, and inherent advantages. The proposed capacitor configuration consolidates the functionalities of multiple 2 or 3-terminal capacitors, addressing challenges in diverse applications. Four distinct scenarios demonstrate the 4-terminal capacitor’s applicability, showcasing advantages such as reduced PCB estate, streamlined assembly, and enhanced SI/EMC performance. This innovative capacitor design represents a promising advancement in electronic components, offering versatility and efficiency across a spectrum of applications.

articleTitle: An Improved Methodology for Passive Channel Signal Integrity Performance Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, the signal integrity (SI) performance on typical passive channels of general servers are studied. An improved solution is proposed to test the SI performance of CPU-to-CPU and CPU-to-MCIO channels using high speed flex-rigid PCBs. Test results show that the proposed method can offer a higher test bandwidth with lower cost and less design difficulties. In addition, good correlation can be obtained between measurement and simulation of the passive channels. Such findings provide a guideline to passive channel design and evaluation of higher data speed applications in the future.

articleTitle: TxRx EMI Experimental Analysis from SNR of Nonlinear Microwave Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: An experimental investigation on the assessment of electromagnetic interference (EMI) influence on the 5G wireless communication system is developed. The proposed EMI analysis is based on the nonlinear (NL) effect of microwave power amplifier (PA) in addition to the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) between the transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) 5G system. The NL effect is quantified with 1-dB compression gain and the third order intermodulation product (IP3). The experimental setup using double frequency injection method modulating QPSK 5G-standard signals is introduced. The IP3 due to the PA NL effect are discussed. The assessed SNR is empirically determined from error vector magnitude (EVM).

articleTitle: A Modeling Method of Receivers for Conducted Emission Noise Test and its Validation with An Electric Vehicle Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: A modeling method of electromagnetic interference (EMI) receivers for conducted emission tests is presented. The method applies a short-time Fourier transform(STFT) to mimic the resolution bandwidth of the EMI receiver. Moreover, the mean and peak detectors can be implemented from the STFT matrix. Finally, an experimental validation is conducted with an electrical vehicle charger.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Electromagnetic Interference Between Electromagnetic Noise from an Autonomous Vehicle and GPS Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles such as drones and self-driving cars have been used in recent years. Many autonomous vehicles use the global positioning system (GPS) to acquire location data, which requires high accuracy. On the other hand, electromagnetic (EM) environment inside the autonomous vehicle is complicated since EM noise sources and a GPS antenna are densely mounted. This environment may degrade the accuracy of positioning measurements by EM interference between EM noise and GPS signals. Previous studies have reported the interference of EM noise with global navigation satellite system (GNSS) and with the mobile communications used by drones. Evaluations and countermeasures for the EM interference problems are necessary since the accuracy degradation of positioning measurements may lead to contact accidents between aircraft. In this study, we evaluated the EM interference between EM noise and GPS signals. There are two setups for the evaluation, the actual setup using a GPS receiver module and the simulation setup. These two evaluation setups were confirmed to be quantitative and reliable by the EM interference evaluation using random noise. Finally, we evaluated the impact of EM interference by EM noise from a commercial drone, one of the autonomous vehicles, on the GPS receiving sensitivity. The sensitivity degraded by about 10 dB in the actual evaluation and by about 11 dB in the simulation evaluation. This result shows that the EM noise from autonomous vehicles has a huge impact on the sensitivity of GPS.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Common Mode Choke for Conducted Noise Reduction from Differential Line to Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Communication capacity is increasing in various markets, and it is desired to increase data transmission speed. Therefore, the use of shielded cables with high frequency characteristics as transmission cables has been studied. However, even in the shielded cable, noise is conducted to the shield layer, which causes a radiation noise problem. Therefore, in this study, the noise conducted to the ground from the differential line is measured, the cause of the noise increase is observed, and the mounting of a countermeasure component for noise reduction is discussed. As a result, it was confirmed that the amount of conducted noise to the ground changed depending on the amount of common mode transmitted to the differential line. Furthermore, the common mode choke (CMC) is mounted, and the conducted noise can be reduced by reducing the common mode. However, it was confirmed that depending on the common mode amount of the differential line, the noise may not be reduced or may be increased depending on the mode conversion characteristics of the CMC.

articleTitle: Multi-point Time Domain Computation for Crosstalk Prediction in Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Determining the ratio of the mutual inductance and mutual capacitance of a multi conductor transmission line (MTL) on a printed circuit board (PCB) such as in the coplanar stripline is important for predicting and mitigating the crosstalk that can occur in the PCB. However, calculating this value directly from the dimension and the material of the PCB can be difficult. This paper describes the multi-point computation method for determining the mutual inductance and mutual capacitance ratio of a coplanar stripline on a PCB. The model was created and simulated in LTSpice. This value is obtained from the near-end and far-end side parameters of the coplanar stripline. The LTspice simulation result shows that the timedomain multi-point computation result from the near-end and far-end voltage and resistance agrees with the direct calculation from the dimension and the material of the coplanar stripline, with 5% tolerance.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Integration of a Symmetrical LCL-EMI Filter for Grid-Connected Voltage-Source Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Switching harmonics and conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) emissions are two challenging issues in grid-tied converters. Utilizing relevant passive filters is a major solution to such issues, these filters enlarge the total volume and weight of the system. Many works have been done to integrate the filtering components to varying degrees. For achieving the highest integration design, this paper proposes an ultimate integration approach of a symmetrical LCL-EMI filter with flexible multilayer foil (FMLF) technique. All the harmonic and EMI suppression components are integrated into the same core unit. A prototype of the proposed integrated filter is built for a 1-kW SiC-MOSFET grid-tied inverter, experiments are carried out to demonstrate the feasibility and superiority of the approach.

articleTitle: Suppression Effect of Ringing in Contact Discharge Waveform from Two Different ESD Generators via Ferrite Core Attached Return Current Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Suppression effects of a 2 m return cable with and without a ferrite core attached to its midpoint on the ringing of contact discharge calibration waveforms are investigated for two different types of ESD generators: one battery-driven and the other AC-driven generators, by comparing the measured waveforms of 4 kV contact discharge currents along with their frequency spectra. The result exhibits that the ringing of the time axis waveforms from both ESD generators can be reduced by attaching the ferrite core to the return cable at the center position compared to the normal return cable, and that the spectral variation around 100 MHz can also be suppressed due to the lower resonance Q (quality factor) values from the measured impedances of the single-ended grounded return cables. Furthermore, for the AC-driven ESD generator with a ferrite-core-attached return cable, when the charging cable is floated, the ringing is found to be significantly mitigated over the entire frequency range from 20 MHz to 200 MHz that the ringing of this kind appears, and both the time axis waveforms and spectra become closer to the IEC specified waveform and spectrum, respectively.

articleTitle: Efficient Terminal Response Simulation of Shielded Cable Excited by an Electromagnetic Plane Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper introduces an efficient method to calculate the terminal response of the shielded cable excited by an electromagnetic plane wave. The method is formulated by deriving the multiconductor transmission line equations of a three-conductor transmission line system encompassing the inner wire, the shield and the ground plane. The terminal response is subsequently determined utilizing the Baum–Liu– Tesche (BLT) equation. The results of the proposed method are consistent with those of conventional approach, while a notable reduction in computational time is realized due to the decrease of overall complexity.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification and Sensitivity Analysis of Crosstalk in PCB Lines via the Combination of Machine Learning and Polynomial Chaos Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Manufacturing tolerances are becoming one of the major limitations to achieving high data rates in modern integrated circuits. Polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) recently became a popular alternative to classical Monte Carlo for efficient uncertainty quantification (UQ). Statistical moments and sensitivity information are analytically derived from the PCE coefficients. However, computing the model coefficients typically requires a large amount of data samples from possibly expensive design simulations. On the other hand, kernel-based machine learning methods were recently employed to create efficient surrogate models with a limited amount of training data. In this paper, we combine the kernel Gaussian process regression (GPR) method and the PCE. The former is used to surrogate the expensive simulator in the calculation of PCE coefficients via numerical integration. The use of GPR also allows obtaining confidence levels of the estimated PCE coefficients and the relative statistical information. The proposed hybrid PCE-GPR method is applied to UQ of maximum crosstalk in a PCB interconnect, for which higher accuracy with a very limited amount of data is obtained compared to state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Round-Robin Test of Site VSWR Validation for 18-40 GHz Band in Japan
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The validation of test sites for EMI measurements in a frequency range between 18 and 40GHz is required. There has been no instruction specified in the CISPR standards for the site validation in this frequency range. However, the site VSIVR measurements might be time consuming and costly. It would be beneficial in the aspect of time and cost if the site validation can be omitted for 18 to 40GHz when the test site is already compliant with the CISPR 16-1-4 specification below 18GHz. This report shows the round-robin test results of the site VSWR for 1-6, 6-18, and 18-40 GHz bands done in six test sites in Japan. The results have shown the possibility to omit the site validation when the test site is already compliant with the CISPR $6 \mathrm{~dB}$ limit in the frequency range below 18GHz.

articleTitle: Investigation of Calculation Accuracy for Line Constants of Transmission Line Constructed With Cable and Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The transmission line constructed with cable and ground plane is one of the radiated emission sources. Therefore, the characteristics of the line should be investigated to achieve electromagnetic compatibility. The numerical analysis has the merit that the characteristics can be investigated effectively, but the perfect modeling of this transmission line is difficult. In this paper, we evaluated the calculation accuracy from 0.1 MHz to 1000 MHz by comparing the calculating line constants with the measuring values. As a result, it was found that the characteristic impedance and phase constant can be calculated with a certain degree of accuracy, but the deviation of the attenuation constant is large.

articleTitle: Hybrid Fast Modeling of Via-Connected Traces in Multilayer Electronic Packages
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Signal conversion between different layers of high-speed interconnect links will cause serious noise and crosstalk problems. This paper presents a hybrid fast modeling approach to efficiently analyze the port conversion of via-connected microstrip and strip lines in multilayer electronic package structures. The results indicate that our method can efficiently analyze the transmission and crosstalk parameters of via-connected traces. Further, the impact of different ground via layouts is presented, which demonstrates a prospect for automatic optimization design.

articleTitle: Considerations for Transient Voltage and Current Induced to Signal Line in Aircraft Bundles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, the analysis of the transient voltage and current induced by the lightning in the aircraft is provided. Some types of aircraft bundle imitated the mal-installation is fabricated and tested. The measurement results show the induced voltage is affected by the shielding and length of the pigtail which is the typical treatment of assembling the physical interface of onboard equipment. The effect of the bundle on the unshielded lines is also evaluated. The result shows the effectiveness of the shield lines bundling with the unshielded line.

articleTitle: Study of a Statistical Risk-Analysis Tool for Evaluating Interference Impact on an ECG Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The latest European Union regulations mandate a risk-based approach to electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). In this context, this study addresses challenges in assessing medical devices’ risk over diverse electromagnetic environments and extended service periods. Combining an ECG signal with waveforms representing various interferences, it explores a novel concept for statistically evaluating interference impact on cyclic biosignals, such as the electrocardiogram (ECG), akin to statistical eye diagrams. The tool offers utility for risk analysis and EMC debugging as it extends insight beyond basic statistical parameters, such as mean or standard deviation, by visualizing the distribution of the total signal for each sample on a unit interval.

articleTitle: A Study on Detectable Conditions for Rusted Reinforcing Bar in Concrete Structure Using a 24-GHz Doppler Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this research, a non-destructive detection method is proposed for the rust on reinforcing bars buried in a concrete structure using a Doppler sensor. The reinforcing bar with the diameter of 9 mm and its corrosion level can be detected by the proposed method. Moreover, the bars buried in mortar wall can be also detected.

articleTitle: Immunity Evaluation Method of Transceiver ICs for In-Vehicle CAN-FD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: It is a well-known fact that a lot of ECUs (Electronic Control Units) and high-speed communication LANs (Local Area Networks) are necessary for ADAS (Advanced Driver Assistance System). OEMs (Original equipment manufacturers) are interested in introducing $C A N$ FD (CAN with Flexible Data Rate) on vehicles for its high data rate. Thereby, CAN-FD is being studied in-vehicle as a replacement for CAN (Controller Area Network). It is expected that many vehicle manufacturers will inherit the conventional CAN components and design policies such as communication lines and ECU design requirements. Accordingly, it is important to determine the immunity performance of the transceiver ICs. In this study, we examined the use of the DPI (Direct Power Injection) Test, which is an immunity test for semiconductors. Focusing on the fact that the main source of error during the BCI (Bulk Current Injection) Test is differential mode noise, and the method is used to select transceiver ICs by generating equivalent differential mode noise in the DPI test.

articleTitle: Estimation of Small Sample EMC Test Data Based on Grey Bootstrap and Uncertain Rational Number
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Under the condition of small sample, a methodology based on Grey Bootstrap and uncertain rational number is employed to data in the determination of EMC compliance of mass-produced products in this article. The experimental data from limited samples undergo resampling using the grey bootstrap method, with additional samples generated through the grey model GM(1,1). An uncertain rational number expression model for virtual samples is established. The point estimation and interval estimation models based on uncertain rational number are introduced, along with corresponding confidence models for correlative estimation. The proposed method is applied to parameter estimation using electromagnetic emission test data for a specific equipment type. The parameters of electromagnetic emission test data for the specified equipment type are estimated through the developed approach. Results from illustrative examples demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits robust estimation reliability without requiring assumptions about the probability distribution of small samples.

articleTitle: Correlation Between Conducted Injection and Near-Field Scan Immunity in the L-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Near-Field Scan Immunity (NFSI) is a recent method for analyzing the electromagnetic (EM) susceptibility of an integrated circuit (IC), allowing the study of a system behavior subject to an intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI). It is a non-intrusive technique that can precisely target component pins that are otherwise inaccessible. This paper compares NFSI to a conducted injection method inspired by the direct power injection (DPI) standard and presents a correlation between the two injection techniques between 500 MHz and 2 GHz. The numerical and experimental validation with different types of near-field probes is validated on passive linear loads.

articleTitle: A Numerical Analysis on Electro-Magnetic Coupling of Printed Circuit Board and High-Frequency Radiated Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic coupling of PCBs and high-frequency radiated field is numerically analyzed using the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. The FD-TD analysis is favorable in handling nonlinear devices like surge protection devices and breakdown phenomena. And the integrated co-simulation with circuit simulator like H-SPICE is available. The coupling voltage in frequency domain was obtained with FDTD method for the PCB in the numerical analysis reported by Louisiana State University and both results were compared. With applying the frequency dependent complex relative permittivity, we got a relatively good agreement. It was shown that the FDTD method is sufficiently applicable to the analysis of the coupling of a high frequency field radiated on PCBs, which will assist in opening the door to the development of an innovative surge protection devices suitable for IEMI protection of microelectronics.

articleTitle: Double screened test setup for discontinuous radiated emissions from GaN HEMT devices in the frequency range of 30 MHz – 40 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This article shows method of measure unwanted radio frequency emission coming from new type transistors constructed on Gallium Nitride base (GaN) in frequency range of 30 MHz - 40 GHz. A dedicated Faraday’s cage was designed to extract emissions coming through housing of the transistor only. Secondary screening was achieved by use of an anechoic chamber and fast wide-band spectrum measurement was taken by real-time EMI receiver.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies About Patch Interval Dependency of as Notch-Filter Properties in Frequency-Selective Sheets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In recent years, frequency discrimination techniques for propagating microwaves have been attracting attention with the spread of wireless systems. One of the convenient notch-filter devices is known as a Frequency-Selective Sheet (FSS) composed of an array of metal patches. Although the control of stopband frequency by metal patch length is well known, the adjustment of stopband width has not been sufficiently studied. In this report, we focus on the effect of patch array interval on the stopband width. Furthermore, based on a large number of measurement results, verification results of the dependency of the stopband width on the patch array interval are described.

articleTitle: Comparison of S-Parameter Low Frequency Interpolation Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: When running time-domain simulations, not having a DC point can cause issues. It is thus necessary to employ methods to extract the low-frequency information and the DC point. In previous literature, methods such as linear, polynomial, and discrete Hilbert integrals have been utilized for interpolation, yet there is a lack of comparative analyses involving diverse low-frequency interpolation methods. In this study, six methods of interpolation are compared, including linear, quadratic, cubic spline, PCHIP, Barycentric, and Akima. Through testing, it is found that (i) when the lowest data point is at 300kHz, there is only a subtle difference among these methods, (ii) in the case of long channels, employing Akima and Barycentric interpolations exhibits more significant discrepancies compared to other methods, and (iii) choosing linear or PCHIP for interpolation in the frequency domain would be a more stable option.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electrical Characteristics of Twinax Cable with Asymmetric Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This work aims to investigate whether the asymmetrical structure impacts performance. The focus is on the mixed mode of the asymmetric twinax cable. Because of the high mesh count in 3D full-wave simulations, they take a long time. To expedite design, a method has been developed to extract twinax cable RLGC parameters, calculate mixed-mode Sparameters, and perform analysis and evaluations. Also, examine common manufacturing imperfections. This research provides an approach to assist cable manufacturers in the rapid design of twinax cable as a simple structural dimension to define the tolerance.

articleTitle: Comparisons of Equalization Performances and CM Suppression on NRZ and PAM4 Signals using Wideband DME-CMF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, the difference between the NRZ signal equalization and the PAM4 signal equalization of a circuit with dual function of differential mode equalizer and common mode filter (DME-CMF) is discussed, and a verification of common mode suppression in time domain is carried out.
