To evaluate NRZ and PAM4 differential equalizations, definitions of effective equalization bandwidth and normalized eye height are proposed and the DME-CMF is proven to maintain a better quality for PAM4 signals than for NRZ signals. For common mode suppression, a time-domain simulation is conducted and a definition of common mode suppression capability is provided to demonstrate that the DME-CMF has significant common mode suppression on both NRZ and PAM4 signals.

articleTitle: Mitigating Crosstalk in High-Speed Digital Interconnect Systems Using High-impedance Surface with Embedded Metal Protrusions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In server systems, the moat or slot is added in the system’s reference plane to suppress Delta-I noise and ground bounce noise. Furthermore, moats in servers aid in distinguishing voltage power and ground planes. However, when a single-ended signal line crosses a slot or moat, parasitic modes, also known as parallel-plate modes (pp-mode), arise due to the discontinuity in the return path in the stripline. This mode results in crosstalk interference at both the near and far ends. Therefore, the proposed solution in this paper is to use a high-impedance surface to suppress the propagation of the parallelplate mode, thereby reducing crosstalk interference. The high-impedance surface operates in the frequency domain at 12.4-14.6 GHz, and this structure achieves a 32% reduction in peak-to-peak crosstalk interference in the time domain.

articleTitle: A New Experimental System for Mechanism Research on Electrostatic Discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: A new experimental system has been invented to simulate the accumulating and dissipating process of electrostatic charges. The efficiency of this system to generate static voltage is high and the repeatability of the voltage value under same conditions is good. So, this system will be very helpful for mechanism research on Electrostatic Discharge.

articleTitle: Causality Assessment of Channels with Long Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Causality is crucial in analyzing frequency responses in long channel systems, where its accurate assessment is challenging. Long delay systems often face numerical errors due to low sampling rates. This paper discusses two scenarios of causality misjudgment and proposes a solution focusing on delay time removal to reduce errors. We introduce a runtime method for delay time estimation, combined with a modified dispersion relation, to enhance the accuracy of causality determination in long channels.

articleTitle: Conducted Noise Emission Analysis of Interleaved Totem-pole Bridgeless PFC Circuit with Power Line Impedance for EV Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: When the PF is low and current distortion in power conversion system is severe, heat is generated in the inductor and transformer containing the magnetic material, and large losses in the power conversion system are generated. Moreover, strict standards for harmonic current are explained in international standards. Even if PFC circuit is added in EV charger to bring its power factor close to one, it has long wires to the power supply, and the inductance of long wires causes low power factor by changed impedance. Because the actual operating state was simulated, the effects of line impedance stabilization network (LISN) was excluded. This paper shows a conducted noise analysis for an interleaved totem pole bridgeless PFC circuit in an EV charger. The conducted noise and its spectrum from EV charger are measured using oscilloscope for verification.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Dependence of Wiring Lengths of Radiated Immunity of Harnesses Connecting Automotive Communication Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, we compared the immunity characteristics of wiring harnesses connecting automotive communication equipment at different wiring lengths. The communication behavior of an automotive harness connected to an evaluation module equipped with automotive Ethernet and exposed to radiated electromagnetic noise was compared for different wiring lengths. The S-parameters were measured under the same wiring conditions, and the frequency characteristics of the amount of noise applied were derived and compared with the length of the wiring. A reverberation chamber was used for the evaluation. From the results of each evaluation, changes in immunity characteristics due to differences in wiring length were confirmed for each frequency of electromagnetic waves, but no correlation was observed between communication quality characteristics and the results of S-parameter measurement. On the other hand, the frequency characteristics of the amount of noise applied also changed with the difference in wiring length, suggesting that a stable evaluation is possible with longer wiring lengths.

articleTitle: Normal and Antenna Mode Coupling Due to Mode Impedance Mismatch in Two-Conductor Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper examines the generation of electromagnetic noise caused by coupling between normal mode (NM) and antenna mode (AM) in a two-conductor transmission line (TL). We derive the telegraph equations for NM and AM using electromagnetic potentials and quantity the coupling effect at the connection of TLs with different mode impedances based on experimental and numerical observations. This study demonstrates that impedance matching of TLs requires the consideration of not only NM impedance but also coupling impedance.

articleTitle: Dual Inductive Probe Concept for Impedance Measurements from 9 kHz to 120 MHz in Presence of High DC-Bias Current - Part Two
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The introduction of fast switching silicon-carbide- or gallium-nitrite-semiconductors allow to build up more efficient power electronic devices, but also lead to shifts in the frequency spectrum regarding to disturbances. Therefore, the knowledge of high frequency properties of such devices is of utmost importance. This publication is the second part of two interconnected papers and presents the measurement performance of a two-in-one inductive probe solution for contact-less, phase-correct impedance measurements and a new approach for calibration standards. The proposed probe allows measurements in the frequency range of 9 kHz to 120 MHz in the presence of DC-bias-current of up to 200 A. Design strategies and the actual design measures are described in first contribution with title “Dual Inductive Probe Concept for Impedance Measurements from 9 kHz to 120 MHz in Presence of High DC-Bias Current - Part One’’.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Front Door Coupling of High Power Microwave to RF Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: High power microwave enters the RF channel through the front door coupling and can cause damage to sensitive devices. This paper designs and simulates a typical RF front-end protection device limiter. The field coupling simulation model of the antenna is used to conduct fieldcircuit co-simulation to analyze the influence of high power microwave signal parameters on the RF channel interference. The simulation method can monitor coupling signal from the antenna port to each node of the back-end circuit under the high power microwave environment. Additionally, it characterizes the actual high power microwave impact of every circuit module, thus enabling a foundation for fieldcircuit co-protection design in a later phase.

articleTitle: Novel Comprehensive Resilience Strategy for Modern Substations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Protection of critical infrastructure has long been paramount to the security and defense of the United States and many countries<sup>[1]</sup>. Traditionally, protection has focused on a narrow approach to either cyber threats, High Altitude Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP), Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) and Intentional Electromagnetic Interference (IEMI), or to more prevalent issues such as small arms ballistics, wind, flooding, and fire that could disrupt supply and delivery. Utilities, for example, have long focused on providing resilience to inclement weather so as to avoid power outages that adversely impact their customers. However, many governments worldwide are now requiring protection of critical infrastructure. For utilities, this most often requires an added layer of protection against cyber threats, HEMP, EMP, and IEMI. This paper describes a novel approach to utilities that provides comprehensive protection of modern substations not only from cyber-attacks, HEMP, EMP, IEMI, and other malicious events, but also from small arms ballistics, wind, flooding, and fire. Utilizing shielding systems capable of providing shielding effectiveness compliant with MIL-STD-188-125 and components that comply with IEC 61850, this paper reviews a resilient substation system that is reliable, cost effective, and easy to install. Further, these systems are compact and can be quickly deployed to a new location providing a comprehensive, flexible, and adaptive solution to hardening substations and transmission stations. A real-world example is provided to document the efficiencies in the comprehensive protection system. While previous papers<sup>[2], [3]</sup> have focused on the design of a substation system, this paper documents long-term performance and extended deployment.

articleTitle: In-circuit Noise Source Impedance Using Double Impedances Insert Loss Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) filter as the most effective method to reduce the conducted EMI. In order to optimize EMI filter to provide effective insertion loss, it is necessary to understand the noise source and the load impedance. In this paper, a double impedance method is proposed to measure and calculate unknowns under interested frequency. First, the effects of noise source impedance on insertion loss are analyzed. Second, the configuration of the proposed method is presented. Finally, the feasibility and accuracy of the method are verified by simulation and experiment. Compared with the previous impedance extraction methods, the proposed approach can obtain the magnitude and the phase of impedances, and it requires no additional equipment.

articleTitle: Impedance Determination of DUT by use of Line Injector Measurement Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper introduces a streamlined method for measuring inline Differential Mode (DM) and Common Mode (CM) impedances of various Device Under Test (DUT) utilizing a line injector. This approach, while straightforward, is more direct than conventional methods that rely on inductive or capacitive coupling. This paper has established a theoretical foundation for this technique, conducting simulations to model the line injector and DUT interactions. The measurements were then compared with data obtained from standard impedance analyzers, demonstrating a clear correlation and emphasizing the efficacy of our method in determining the impedance of a DUT.

articleTitle: Withstand Performance of Varistors Against High Altitude Electromagnetic Pulse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In recent years, the widespread use of sensitive electronic device has heightened the risk of component damage from external electromagnetic fields. For example, intense electromagnetic fields in the frequency range of 200 MHz to 5GHz are known to cause upset or damage to electronic systems [1]. In this paper, multilayer varistors, employed particularly as protective components against EMC problems associated with electrostatic discharges (ESD), are evaluated assuming invasion of High Altitude Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP). In particular, this study focuses on evaluation of degradation characteristics of multilayer varistors subjected to early-time HEMP-type conducted IEMI pulses.

articleTitle: Functionality Introduction of Japanese Customized ILS Simulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of an instrument landing system (ILS) simulator developed by the Electronic Navigation Research institute (ENRI). The developed simulator is mainly used for treating Japanese environments. To minimize computer memory as much as possible, the raytracing method (RTM) was used as a numerical method for visualizing propagation path and electric field distribution.

articleTitle: Noise Coupling Prediction Inside a Small Shielding Box Based on Phaseless Near-Field Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, a novel algorithm is proposed to predict the noise coupling between the electromagnetic interference (EMI) source and victim inside the same shielding box. Firstly, the unknown EMI source and victim are represented by equivalent dipoles. The phaseless near-fields radiated from the EMI source and victim under transmitting mode are used to construct the equivalent dipoles. To accurately consider the effect of the shielding box on the equivalent dipoles, the leaked near-fields from the shielding box are used to adjust the moments of the constructed dipoles. Furthermore, the Norton/Thevenin equivalent circuit of the victim is developed, where the excitation current/voltage is obtained by using the reciprocity theorem. Measurement results show the accuracy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Conducted Emission Simulation with ICEM Modeling and Measurement for HV Buck Integrated Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Since recently developed smart devices and automotive electronics largely depend upon the power consumption control and converting efficiency, power management integrated circuits (PMIC) become necessary and more demanding to the system performance. However, the more severe switching noise emitted unintentionally from the highly efficient PMIC has also given rise to electromagnetic interference (EMI) problems within the device. Recent studies have shown that IC noise is the root cause of EMI problems during system integration, therefore the studies of IC-EMC would reveal the most effective solutions for suppressing EMI noise by measuring and analyzing the key issue of IC operation. With the IC EMI characteristic behavior, the IC manufacturers and their customers for system development will benefit to achieve product compliance in the early design stage. This study is based upon the current probe method of IEC 61967-4 [1] Standard for conducting electromagnetic emission measurement at the chip level of High-Voltage Buck IC for further EM model simulation. We will then generate the Chip Power Modeling (CPM) behavior model of the PMIC by utilizing the ANSYS Totem tool and implementing the EM characteristics of the related evaluation board to proceed with the EMI simulation on board level according to the ICEM-CE modeling of IEC 62433-2. We will then finally compare the conducted EMI results from measurement and simulation to analyze the effect of PMIC switching activity. The methodology described in this study for chip-level EMI analysis will be helpful in the early IC design stage for EMI problem resolution to reduce the development cycle and cost.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification in PEEC Method: A Physics-Informed Neural Networks-Based Polynomial Chaos Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to uncertainty quantification (UQ) in the partial equivalent element circuit (PEEC) method through a physics-informed neural networks (PINNs)-based polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) scheme. Initially, the PEEC method is formulated via the electrical field integral equations and continuity equations. Subsequently, random parameters are introduced to construct stochastic equations, generating input and output observations for training data. The PCE method is then employed to establish a mapping function. To calculate the coefficients of polynomial bases, a PINNs-based method is applied, utilizing the constructed matrix derived from the training data. Finally, this methodology enables the determination of stochastic parameters for quantities of interest within the PEEC method. The numerical example involving a transmission line is provided to verify the efficiency of the proposed method. It is found that the uncertainty is well quantified in all cases.

articleTitle: Circuit Modeling of Arbitrary Crystal Oscillator for EMC and SI Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Quartz crystal oscillators are fundamental components in electronic circuits with stringent time requirements; providing a proper crystal oscillator model for simulation is crucial for Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) and Signal Integrity (SI) analysis. This paper presents two types of behavioral models of quartz oscillators for EMC-oriented circuit simulations. These behavioral models allow the oscillator to be simulated without the need to resort to the complete oscillator circuit. The proposed models are tested in simulation of four oscillators, operating at different frequencies. These models provide a tool for early-stage analysis of EMC and SI performance in electronic systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetic Core Winding of Inductive Coupler for Pulsed Current Injection(PCI)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Pulsed current injection (PCI) is an essential method to investigate the effects of electromagnetic pulse, and the investigation of its coupling mode has become an area of significant interest within the EMC industry. The paper concentrates on the magnetic core winding of the inductive coupler for PCI. Based on the permeability curve of the nanocrystalline obtained from the test, the effects of parameters such as the size and coil of the magnetic core winding on the performance of the coupler are analyzed by simulation models. Finally, suggested design requirements that are relevant to PCI inductive coupler are presented.

articleTitle: Modeling Power-Bus Structures with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper presents electromagnetic modeling of power-bus structures with physics-informed neural networks. A deep neural network (DNN) is used as a solution surrogate to the Helmholtz equation describing a physical law of voltage distributions in the parallel-plate structures. Its equation is directly embedded in the loss function of the DNN to be trained. The developed method can be regarded to be data-free and mesh-free. It is applied to the analysis of input impedance of a circular power-bus structure with dielectric and conductor losses. The predicted result is verified in comparison with the theoretical one.

articleTitle: Effects of Ionising Radiation on the Electromagnetic Immunity Behaviour of Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, we analyse the impact of ionising radiation on the conducted electromagnetic immunity of integrated circuits (ICs). We use the direct power injection (DPI) method according to IEC 62132-4 to characterize the conducted electromagnetic immunity of our test IC at the VDD pin. In addition to measuring the electromagnetic immunity, we irradiate the IC with X-rays. The irradiation process is carried out up to a dose of 1.5Mrad using a high power X-ray radiation source. The electromagnetic immunity characteristic of the IC is determined for the unirradiated IC and for doses of 0.5Mrad, 1.0Mrad and 1.5Mrad. We present measurement results demonstrating a low but significant impact of ionising radiation on the conducted electromagnetic immunity behaviour of our test IC. With increasing radiation dose, our IC is getting more robust towards radio frequency interference (RFI) at the VDD pin.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity Analysis and Design for Cascaded Wire Bonding of Low-Power Double Data Rate (LPDDR)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, the cascaded wire bonding is analyzed in terms of signal integrity and the design strategy is presented for improving the signaling performance. Cascaded wire boding has emerged according to the demand for integrating more functionalities in vertical stacking semiconductor devices. However, the signal flowing along the cascaded wire bonding structure faces signal degradation due to complex multiple reflections. We analyze the signaling characteristic of cascaded wire bonding in frequency and time domain respectively with a simple methodology that adopts an ideal transmission line segment model. This analysis entails the condition of wire bonding length and termination to infer optimal design conditions. Based on complementary analysis results, the design guide for optimal cascaded wire bonding is presented.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Issues of Aircraft Radio Altimeters Due to Sub-6 Band 5G Mobile Communications Systems in Japan
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues of the aircraft radio altimeter (RA) due to Sub-6 band 5G mobile communication system in Japan is discussed based on the experimental results. Sub-6 band 5G mobile commutation systems have been adopted globally. However, in Japan, the guard band between RAs and 5G mobile commutation systems is 100 MHz, which is lower than that in most other countries. In this study, we investigated EMI in aircraft RAs due to Sub-6 band 5G mobile communication systems in Japan. First, the EMI characteristics of RAs are measured under a narrow guard band. Next, the interference tolerance mask (ITM) is calculated from the measured interference thresholds. Finally, the obtained ITMs are compared with those reported under wider guard bands. The results confirm that Japan has a higher risk of interference than the United States and France because of the narrower guard band in Japan.

articleTitle: Oblique Incident Reflection Characteristic Evaluation of EM Wave Absorber for 28 GHz Without Metal Backing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The oblique incidence characteristics of an electromagnetic wave absorber for 28GHz with a structure consisting of a conductive material layer and a dielectric material layer were evaluated analytically and experimentally. By optimizing the design of the conductor layer, it was confirmed that the difference in the properties at oblique incidence between with/without metal backing was little. The reflection coefficient with increasing incident angle was different between the TE and TM incident waves. Then, the polar chart was used to investigate. Matching conditions (reflectance coefficient was less than 0.1) were obtained in the angle range up to about 60° for TE incident waves. An electromagnetic wave absorber without metal backing using this structure has advantages in terms of cost, weight and flexibility in the millimeter wave band.

articleTitle: Characterization of Architectural Glasses by Free-Space Method in 24 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The leakage from an indoor 24 GHz power transmission systems through window glasses is concerned. Although ray tracing simulation is effective for the leakage simulation, there are not many reports on the transmission characteristics and complex permittivities of the glasses. In this study, the transmission characteristics of three representative types of architectural glasses were measured in 24 GHz band by the free space method. As a result, the shielding performances of Low-E glasses were 19 - 33 dB at 24 GHz. The measured relative dielectric constants and dielectric loss tangents of float glasses fabricated by several manufacturers were about $6.9 \pm 0.05$ and $0.02 \pm 0.003$, respectively at 24 GHz.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a Non-Intrusive SDR-Based in-situ Shielding Effectiveness Measurement Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: An assessment of the instrumentation to be employed for in-situ shielding effectiveness (SE) measurements in 3D complex structures is carried out in this paper. The proposed methodology, based on an inside-out technique, makes use of non-intrusive and portable instruments, with a small foot-print. The limitations of the SDR-based instruments used is evaluated and their impact on the final measured value is discussed. A closed-loop measuring setup was proposed to make a preliminary investigation of the instruments performance in a highly controlled environment. This is supplemented by an examination of an averaging post-processing technique and its influence on the measured SE value. Although inside-out testing is not generally employed, it may be used as the basis for a unsophisticated SE evaluation technique.

articleTitle: Dust Figure Guided Modeling of Corona Discharge on Touchscreen Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electrostatic discharge to a touchscreen display leads to a corona discharge which creates corona streamers that| propagate along the glass surface. The streamers couple energy to touch sensors underneath the glass which may then cause failure. Modeling the ionized air resistance and the current distribution on the glass surface from corona discharge is challenging. A new methodology is proposed for modeling corona discharge to a touchscreen surface with the help of experimentally measured dust figures. A geometric analysis of the dust figure and how streamer currents couple to the sensor patch matrix is given to explain the modeling method. A SPICE model is proposed to better correlate the ESD gun current with the current coupled to the sensor patches. The ability of the model to predict peak current, charge and rise time is evaluated. Predictions of peak current and charge are within 30% error.

articleTitle: Impedance Dependencies of TVS Diode’s Response Against ESD Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The protection performance of an electrostatic-discharge (ESD) protection device may differ from one device to another, even if the specifications are equivalent. Additionally, the performance of an ESD-protection device changes when implemented in different circuit impedances or external connection device. Therefore, this study aims to clear the influence of circuit impedances on the performance of ESD-protection devices. First, we measured the response voltage waveform under five different resistances using three types of TVS diode with the same breakdown voltage specification. Second, we analyzed the clamping duration and the time constant of the voltage drop after the clamping operation. We compared these characteristics among the three types of TVS diode. The results showed that the clamping duration and the time constant would be longer under a higher circuit impedance. The difference among TVS diodes will be more distinct as the impedance increases, even when the breakdown voltage specifications of the TVS diode are equivalent.

articleTitle: Novel Power Grid Design Architecture to Improve IR Voltage Drop and EMI Shield
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: With technology shrinking and increasing functionality leading to high power consumption, today’s System-on-Chip (SoC) requires new power distribution network (PDN) design in BEOL layers to meet IR voltage drop. In the conventional approach, the PDN is designed with multiple metal and via layers which are very resistive and cannot support more than $\sim 2-3 A$ of current consumption with wire-bond packages with required IR voltage drop limit (e.g. $\lt 10 \%$). To support higher power consumption of SoC Applications, one needs to design with 3-4 dedicated thick metal layers of BEOL to design PDN in addition to a flip chip package which leads to higher wafer and package cost. For $16 \mathrm{~nm}$ and below technology nodes, Back-End-Of-Line (BEOL), Middle-Of-Line (MOL) and the package are becoming more critical in driving and shaping the chip and system level PPA (Power, Performance, Area) improvement. In this paper, two methods are proposed for novel power grid architecture design. One is fully-Platted-Power Grid (PPG) design and the other one is partially-Platted Power Grid (PPPG) design to improve IR voltage drop enabling higher chip power consumption and improving Electro-Magnetic Interference shielding (EMI Shield) using wire bond package to reduce wafer cost and package cost by avoiding flip chip package.

articleTitle: Electronic Board Emission Model and its Application for Microcontroller Emission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In the evaluation of system-level electromagnetic emission, it is important to model emission contributions from individual electronic boards. This paper presents a methodology to obtain an electronic board emission model (EBEM) using a measurement-based, top-down approach. It involves modeling the activity causing the emission as a current source, and a source impedance. We propose a method for the measurement of the s-parameter of the board and further de-embedding the overall test fixture to get the impedance of the board alone. We provide an analytical formulation for calculating the current source from the conducted emission test setup. The combined source and impedance model is used to predict the emission from the same electronic board in different environments. The method is developed for the STM32 microcontroller board and the methodology is validated through measurements.

articleTitle: Dual Inductive Probe Concept for Impedance Measurements from 9 kHz to 120 MHz in Presence of High DC-Bias Current - Part One
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The introduction of fast switching silicon-carbide-or gallium-nitrite-semiconductors allow to build up more efficient power electronic devices, but also lead to shifts in the frequency spectrum regarding to disturbances. Therefore, the knowledge of high frequency properties of such devices is of utmost importance. This paper presents design rules, construction details of a two-in- one inductive probe solution for contact-less, phase-correct impedance measurements and a new approach for calibration standards. The proposed probe allows measurements in the frequency range of 9 kHz to 120 MHz in the presence of DC-biascurrents of up to 200 A. In a second contribution with the title ”Dual Inductive Probe Concept for Impedance Measurements from 9 kHz to 120 MHz in Presence of High DC-Bias Current - Part Two” the performance of the described probe is discussed.

articleTitle: Numerical Evaluation of ElectroMagnetic Effects for Different Types of Shield Connection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This article describes a numerical evaluation of the electromagnetic (EM) effects for different types of shielding connection based on the transmission line formalism. Previous work on EWIS (Electrical Wiring InterConnect System) has highlighted the influence of different shielding connections on the stresses induced in internal conductors, and more particularly the importance of fully modeling pigtails as transmission lines, considered as sensors of the incident EM field and likely to couple with internal conductors.

articleTitle: Calibration of Broadband Antenna Using the Standard Field Method With VNA Considering the Near Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: We proposed a standard electric field method using a VNA with an equation that takes into account the nearfield conditions of the electric field radiated from the transmitting antenna and compensates for the effect of the input power reflection of the transmitting antenna. Furthermore, the absolute gain of a conical monopole antenna with doubleBoltzmann tapered-line (DB-CMA) upto 20 GHz was measured using this method. As a result, although the average absolute gain of DB-CMA from 1 GHz to 20 GHz was slightly lower than that of tuned monopole, the DB-CMA has a broadband property and is suitable for measuring transient electromagnetic fields such as ESD electromagnetic fields.

articleTitle: Noise Suppression Sheet Embedded in Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: To mitigate the electromagnetic interference issues which deteriorate the mobile communication performance of UAV’s, soft magnetic noise suppression sheets (NSSs) are embedded inside printed circuit boards (PCBs) used in a commercial drone. For the PCBs with embedded NSS, reduction of near-field noise was observed by around 10dB.

articleTitle: Proposal of Components level Test for HPEM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The use of electronic devices continues to expand in various environments. It is expected that the use of UAVs in extreme environments will be promoted for safety reasons. In this study, we will discuss the need for testing at the system level, module level, and device level in order to confirm safety and prevent failures using the use of UAVs in thunderclouds, and take appropriate countermeasures. We will discuss the importance of establishing test methods at the device level.

articleTitle: Revision Status and Further Study Issue of International Standard on System Level ESD Immunity Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: An international standard of ESD immunity testing is under revising. A major issue in the standard revision is suppressing ringing in the contact discharge current waveform. Many improvement proposals have been made so far, but no solution has yet been found despite much discussion.

articleTitle: Analysis of Degradation of Transmission Characteristics of Underwater Antenna due to Metal Enclosure of Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The Autonomous Underwater Vehicle (AUV) is anticipated as a means of collecting underwater visual information using its built-in camera. While underwater radio wave communication via underwater antennas has been developed as a means of information collection, it is expected that the metal casing of AUV may adversely affect the transmission characteristics of antennas in underwater radio wave communication. Therefore, this report evaluates the impact of AUV’s metal casing on antenna-to-antenna communication using an electromagnetic field simulator. The evaluation indicates that when the size of the antennas is larger than the AUV’s metal casing, the impact on transmission characteristics is minimal even when the AUV is positioned between the antennas. On the other hand, when the metal casing is larger than the antenna size, the transmission characteristics between antennas degrade due to eddy currents flowing in the metal casing induced by antenna currents. Consequently, it is suggested that when attaching underwater antennas to AUVs, maintaining relatively good transmission characteristics, even with smaller antennas, is possible by appropriately configuring the size relationship and placement of the metal casing relative to the antennas.

articleTitle: Development of Passive Common-Noise Canceller Placed on DC Side of Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper reports on the common-mode (CM) voltage suppression of a passive common-noise canceller (PCC), which can cancel the CM noise generated by inverters. The proposed PCC is characterized by the installation position to the DC side of an inverter instead of the AC side. Compared to the conventional AC-side PCC, the proposed PCC can reduce the window area of the CM transformer, so that the size and weight of the PCC can be reduced. This paper describes the design of the PCC and shows experimental CM voltage suppression effect with a voltage-source PWM inverter with SiC-MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Analysis of Radiated Emission in High-Voltage Junction Box Using Conductive Plastic Material in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electric vehicles commonly incorporate lightweighting measures in various key areas. Recently, the trend extends beyond the body structure, chassis, and suspension to include the use of lightweight materials for Power Electric (PE) Components. This paper specifically analyzes the Radiated Emission(RE) issues that arise when utilizing conductive plastic-the lightweight material-in the high voltage junction box. The paper conducts an analysis and comparison of the radiation emitted by HVPE components and the radiation from cables, including the ground wire. Additionally, study is conducted on how to reduce the radiation noise when using the conductive plastic.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Near-field Disturbance on Secondary Equipment of 500kV Series Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The secondary equipment of the series compensation device has the functions of measurement, control and protection, and its working state is closely related to the reliability of the series compensation device. However, when the ground fault occurs, the electromagnetic environment in the area of the series compensation device is abnormally bad, which will bring challenges to the electromagnetic compatibility design of the secondary equipment. Taking the Wanquan series compensation substation in China as an example, this paper studies the impact of near-field disturbance caused by ground fault on the secondary equipment of the series compensation device. The results show that the -15V power port is the most sensitive, which may lead to abnormal operation of the secondary equipment. This work guides the electromagnetic compatibility design of the secondary equipment of the series compensation device.

articleTitle: Conducted Emission Evaluation of 1000BASE-RH Optical Ethernet Transceivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: To clarify the major sources of RF emission from optical Ethernet transceivers, EMC test boards for 1000BASERH 1 Gbps optical Ethernet transceiver ICs and FOTs are fabricated, and conducted RF emission is evaluated. Payload data dependency and emission spectra related to SGMII/ RGMII on respective RF coupling ports at DC supply domains are evaluated.

articleTitle: DVOR - Evaluation and Improvement of the Original Scattering Model and Practical Implications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This contribution presents a discussion of the analytical receiver model, which Anderson et. al. presented in 1959 for the navigation system Doppler VOR in order to describe the bearing deviation due to a static, non-dynamic, and omnidirectional scatterer. To do so, it highlights the used approximations, relates the former results to the intended purpose and highlights pitfalls, which are possible by applying graphs of reduced intelligence in the timely context of wind turbines as scattering objects. Furthermore, the analytical model is improved and compared with Anderson’s model.

articleTitle: Optimal Common Mode Target Impedance for Conducted Emission Noise Suppression in Motor Driver Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Although the traditional inverter/SMPS circuit for home appliances or automobiles has a long history, unexpected common mode noise problems when implemented increase development time and cost. In this paper, we proposed a concept of a common mode target impedance based EMC design methodology to optimally suppress conducted emission(CE) noise and reduce the cost and time consumption. The proposed target impedance can be extracted by measurement of common mode impedance and CE spectrum. By designing common mode impedance based on the proposed target impedance, EMC debugging process can be minimized and unnecessary overdesign can be prevented. A motor driver circuit of a washing machine is designed using the target impedance. It is verified that the CE spectrum can be satisfied the standard with 7.5 dB margin.

articleTitle: Accelerated EMC Site Validation Testing From 30 MHz to 200 MHz With a Reduced Number of Measurement Heights Using the Matrix Pencil Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: EMC test sites undergo compliance testing according to standards such as CISPR 16-1-4 or ANSI C63.4. In the frequency range of 30MHz to 1 GHz, measurements involve acquiring a series of s 21 responses between a fixed-height transmit antenna and o height-scanning antenna (ranging from 1 m to 4 m) over a conductive ground plane. To achieve accurate site validation results, a step size of 5 cm or smaller for the height-scanning antenna is necessary. Performing the required suite of site attenuation measurements, covering two polarizations, different transmit antenna heights, and various positions within a quiet zone, is time-consuming. In this study, we propose employing a larger height increment, such as 10 cm or 15 cm, for collecting height-scanning data. The coarsely measured data is then fitted to a vector function using the Matrix Pencil (MP) method. The results demonstrate that highly comparable outcomes can be achieved with significantly fewer measurement heights, resulting in a substantial reduction in test time without compromising the accuracy and integrity of the measurements.

articleTitle: Circuit Modeling and Simulation of EMI Filter for High Current Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper shows a circuit model that can accurately simulate the differential-mode and common-mode attenuation characteristics of a three-stage EMI filter connected to high-current power converters. Passive components such as common mode choke coils and capacitors are modeled as high-frequency equivalent circuits based on impedance measurement results. For the coils that exhibited characteristics that are difficult to fit manually, vector fitting is used to derive a highly accurate equivalent circuit. The mutual inductance between input and output loops, which has a significant impact on common mode characteristics, is calculated based on the results of electromagnetic field analysis using a 3D CAD model. The combined circuit simulation model is able to predict the filter attenuation characteristics with an accuracy of less than 10 dB error for both modes.

articleTitle: A Resonant Magnetic Field Probe With Enhanced Sensitivity Using Quarter-wavelength Impedance Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, a novel resonant magnetic probe is proposed. The resonance of the probe is achieved by a parallel-plate and metal loop, which provides the parasitic capacitor C and inductor L respectively. Moreover, a quarter-wavelength high impedance line is proposed and inserted into the transmission part of the probe. This line introduces additional multi-reflections along the probe transmission part. Under the optimize line length, such multi-reflections will enhance the output voltage of the probe. Numerical and measurement results show that the sensitivity of the proposed probe can be increased by more than 10 dB at a resonant frequency of 1.575 GHz, in comparing with the reference wideband probe.

articleTitle: Research on Background Noise Test Method of EV-Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In recent years, with the development of the new four modernization of automobiles, the function of the automotive electromagnetic compatibility anechoic chamber has also undergone great changes, such as the EMC anechoic chamber of new energy high-voltage components needs to introduce the transmission system and high-voltage power supply system into the traditional anechoic chamber. However, for this project, there is currently no perfect way to verify that the background noise meets the test requirements of at least 6 dB below the standard limit. This paper introduces an EVChamber background noise test method for electromagnetic compatibility, which is used for EV-Chamber background noise verification, and provides a new idea and method for the industry to improve background noise testing.

articleTitle: Wireless Communication System Use in Medical Hospitals and Management of the Electromagnetic Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: More than 90% of Japanese hospitals have installed wireless LANs and 80% of them have Wireless Medical Telemetry Systems (WMTS). Wireless communication has become an important part of the infrastructure of modern hospitals, and voice communication systems have become indispensable as communication tools. Unfortunately, there have been communication failures caused by inappropriate implementation of wireless communication systems or by a poor electromagnetic environment, such as from electromagnetic noise. Inappropriate information sharing of the materials used in hospital construction is also a factor that causes problems. In this paper, we describe the use of wireless communication in Japanese hospitals, identify problems and their causes, and describe the required countermeasures by referring two Japanese guidelines.

articleTitle: Time-resolved high frequency near-magnetic field imaging system using magneto-optical effect and femto-second laser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: We constructed high frequency near-magnetic field measurement system composed of time-resolved magneto-optical effect measurements with femtosecond lasers and magnetic garnet thin films. The system can measure the magnetic field in an arbitrary phase of MSL because the laser pulses are synchronized with the signal generator. As a high frequency response of Faraday rotation of magnetic garnet thin film with in-plane isotropic easy axes was evaluated using microstrip line (MSL), the Faraday rotation angle of approximately 0.6 mdeg. even at 40GHz was confirmed. In addition, we visualized the clear distribution in $300 \times 100 \mu \mathrm{m}$ area near the center of the line for high-frequency near-magnetic field including phase information when signal at 40 GHz are applied to MSL.

articleTitle: An Approach to the Problem of Balancing a Symmetrical Antenna Circuit Fed by Symmetrical and Asymmetrical Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The interpretation of the concept of balanced circuit feeding and the practical use of balancing often cause difficulties. This includes the antenna circuit of a symmetrical antenna. The paper attempts to approach the problem of balanced feeding of such a circuit. Methods of balanced feeding have been analyzed. Examples of feeding shielded symmetrical lines using a symmetrical generator and an asymmetrical generator with a balun were considered. The use of an asymmetrical coaxial line fed from an asymmetrical generator, feeding the antenna directly and via a balun, was considered. The advantages of using a magneto-dielectric absorber were pointed out, allowing to effectively improve the balancing parameters of an antenna circuit with a balun. Due to the widespread use of coaxial lines with baluns to feed symmetrical antennas, the use of absorber cables (coaxial cables with absorption coating) can potentially be very useful.

articleTitle: Neural Network for the Prediction of Electric Field Intensity Applied to a Simple Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In response to the escalating challenges in Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) driven by the increase of electronic devices, the risk based approach is made mandatory in the EMC Directive. Showing the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly neural networks (NN), in EMC, this paper explores how NNs can be used for a specific case study of predicting the behaviour of the electric field in a simple scenario. The dataset was created by using Full-wave modeling software. Multiple assumptions and steps are taken for the creation of the NN and the adaptation of such a case study to this research. The results show the performance of the NN for different cases in which the model can make good predictions and when it lacks accuracy.

articleTitle: The Impact of Choosing Different Reference Impedances on Calibration Results
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The reference impedance ($z_{\mathrm{r}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{f})}$ of an S parameter after calibration is important for evaluating the quality of a device-under-test (DUT), because it represents the characteristic impedance of the transmission line under which the scattered waves from the DUT are observed. Thus, the value of $Z_{\mathrm{r}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{f}}$ should be clearly known and defined, or the calibration results will be irrelevant. In the current USB and PCIE Specifications, however, the $Z_{\mathrm{r}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{f}}$ is sometimes not clearly defined which can lead to ambiguities in the calibration process. In this paper, the influence of a small change in $Z_{\mathrm{r}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{f}}$ on the calibrated S parameters is analyzed, and experiment is carried out to show the significant impact on return loss. The results reveal the importance of specifying the value of $Z_{\mathrm{r}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{f}}$ precisely, and the characteristic impedance of the calibration kits should be regulated strictly.

articleTitle: Efficient Shielding of the Noise Coupling to the Grid Cable in Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Inthis paper, an investigation of parasitic coupling from the motor cable to the grid cable in motor drives and its mitigation aspects using field shielding technique are presented. A simple and efficient L-shape shielding is proposed and validated using real-life test setup showing very good performance of the proposed solution. Current investigation has been applied to the CM noise mitigation, which usually dominates in motor drives. However, the same principle is equally valid for DM noise mitigation, caused by parasitic cable coupling.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Assessment of a Protection Relay in Electrical Substation to Radiated Intentional EMI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Smart power grid has adopted digital protection relays in electrical substations, but it has also increased the vulnerability of an electrical substation should an intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI) attack happens. Using a commercially available digital protection relay as a case study, radiated susceptibility tests are performed to investigate its susceptibility behaviors. With a known susceptibility level, the numerical model of a 22kV substation is constructed to assess the vulnerability of the protective relays deployed in the substation. It reveals that with the recent development of highpower radio frequency (RF) and microwave sources, the substation could be at risk from an IEMI attack, and thus early mitigation measures should be implemented to minimize such a risk.

articleTitle: Weighting of interference through the ages of radio
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Appropriate weighting of interference is the key for adequate radio protection. The need for radio protection arose with the introduction of AM broadcasting in the 1920s. Numerous interference complaints from radio listeners made radio frequency interference (RFI) suppression necessary for existing electrical devices and equipment, but suitable measurement procedures and instruments were not yet available. Systematic research for defining uniform measurement procedures to protect broadcasting started only after the establishment of the International Special Committee on Radio Interference (CISPR) in 1933. The aim was to keep RFI suppression costs low, which meant RFI suppression should only be applied where relevant.

articleTitle: EMI Noise Analysis Using Frequency Domain Simulation Considering Dynamic Semiconductor Characteristics in Flyback Converter Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: We propose a hybrid analysis method that uses a general SPICE simulator to perform high-speed and high-precision conduction noise analysis of flyback converter circuits. Time domain analysis, generally used for conducted noise analyses, is disadvantaged by its long analysis time. Frequency domain analysis, which requires a shorter analysis time, is also used for conducted noise analyses, but it struggles to reproduce the operating characteristics of semiconductors. The hybrid analysis method enables frequency domain analysis that considers semiconductor operating characteristics by using the results of a time domain analysis as a noise source. The results of our proposed hybrid analysis method matched the results of a time domain analysis across the entire analyzed bandwidth, from $1-100 \mathrm{MHz}$. The analysis time was about $1/10$ of that of the time domain analysis.

articleTitle: Volume Reduction of Traction Power Inverter EMI Filter Based on Mitigation Techniques at the Source
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Switching converters require effective EMI filters to comply with conducted emission regulations. However, these filters often pose significant challenges, being expensive, bulky and heavy. The situation is further exacerbated with the latest generation of converters, utilizing WBG semiconductor devices, which operate at higher switching frequencies. Reduction of the filter size can be achieved through conducted EMI mitigation techniques that address emissions at the source, particularly at low frequencies. This paper analyzes the CM filter volume reduction when using two CM mitigation techniques acting at the source, namely Spread Spectrum Modulation (SSM) and the Delay Compensation Technique (DCT). The considered techniques are implemented on a WBG traction power inverter and the volume reduction of the CM EMI filter is evaluated through computer simulations.

articleTitle: Direct Current Mode Stirred, a Road Map to a New EMC Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper outlines the already conducted and planned activities to get the Direct Current Mode Stirred (DCMS) EMC test method into an applicable EMC standard. The different test objects, as well as test facilities, are outlined and a deeper view into the computational electromagnetics is granted. The major challenge of DCMS lies in the conversion process between the injected power into a test object and the calculation of an equivalent external field strength arising from the resultant surface current on the test object’s skin. A simple theorem, that already achieves a good initial approximation is proposed in the last chapter. Furthermore, some drawbacks of DCMS are mentioned, like different Eigenmodes or parasitic standing waves, although these are not yet included in this straightforward theorem.

articleTitle: A Quantitative Channel Pre-Evaluation Method using Eye Aperture for Low-Power Double Data Rate (LPDDR)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a quantitative channel pre-evaluation method using eye aperture for low-power double data rate (LPDDR). Complex overlapping signal performance was decomposed into three degradation factors by step responses; degradation due to RC delay, inter-symbol interference (ISI), and crosstalk. The total degradation of the eye aperture is quantitatively evaluated based on the approximated degradation factors. The proposed evaluation method is verified for single and 8-coupled channels in the discrete PKG channel environment of LPDDR. We analyze the effect of degradation according to each channel variable.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Compatibility Validation Scheme for ADAS in Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The high level of integration in the power control unit of electric vehicles facilitates the seamless integration of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) into the vehicle’s electronic architecture. However, as the complexity of the electromagnetic environment both inside and outside the vehicle increases, the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) validation of ADAS becomes crucial. Reverberation chamber can simulate complex and random electromagnetic fields within a defined area, providing comprehensive validation of the safety and stability of ADAS. Nevertheless, conventional physical simulation methods face limitations in the confined space of reverberation chamber during ADAS testing. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an EMC validation scheme for ADAS in reverberation chamber based on millimeter-wave radar simulation and visual projection. The proposed method has been validated to successfully activate the vehicle’s ADAS and conduct EMC testing.

articleTitle: Varistor Voltage Behavior of Metal Oxide Varistors Stressed by Electromagnetic Pulse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper describes degradation characteristics of Metal-oxide-varistors (MOVs) stressed by electromagnetic pulses (EMPs). Degradation characteristics under sub-microsecond pulses such as $1/100\mathrm{~ns}$ (TLP), $5/50\mathrm{~ns}$ (EFT/B) and $25/500\mathrm{~ns}$ are confirmed and compared with a lightning impulse current of $8/20\mu\mathrm{s}$. The varistor voltage $V_{0.01\mathrm{~ms}}$ at current 0.01 mA changes asymmetrically dependent on the direction of measurement current under repetitive sub-microsecond shots, similar to $V_{\text{lmA}}$ in the case of application of $8/20\mu\mathrm{s}$ impulses. Degradation of $V_{\operatorname{lmA}}$ is also observed, however, the change of voltage $V_{0.01\mathrm{~mA}}$ is much more sensitive. The degradation of voltages $V_{0.01\mathrm{~mA}}$ and $V_{1\mathrm{~mA}}$ progressed by repetitive sub-microsecond pulse applications, though, the failure of the tested varistor of $4\mathrm{~mm}$ in diameter and $1\mathrm{~mm}$ in thickness did not occur by application of 650 shots of $300-\mathrm{A}$ sub-microsecond pulses with 25/500 ns waveform.

articleTitle: Augmented Genetic Algorithm v3 for Multi-Objective PDN Decap Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for generating the initial population, termed disproportionate initialization, to enhance the genetic algorithm’s efficiency in optimizing the number of decaps. This method is specifically designed to accelerate convergence, improving the algorithm’s ability to find optimal solutions. The algorithm is improved to simultaneously reduce the number of decoupling capacitors and achieve the lowest cost, aiming to identify the global minima for comprehensive PDN optimization.

articleTitle: Closed-Loop Structure for Mitigating Jitter-Induced Noise of Clock Source in High-Bandwidth Signal Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The phase-modulated signal is widely used in current high-performance sensor systems. Due to the high-dynamic signal sensing and detection scenario, optimal system performance demands that the analog-to-digital converter (ADC) exhibits high-bandwidth and low-noise sampling capabilities. As the signal bandwidth expands, elevated jitter levels and poor phase noise with spur interference on the sampling clock will cause non-negligible jitter-induced noise. In this paper, we propose a closed-loop sampling structure to mitigate the jitter-induced noise from the perspective of compressing the signal bandwidth before sampling, thus reducing the noise coupling factor from the sampling clock. The simulation results demonstrate that both the increased noise floor and unwanted spurs due to the jitter-induced noise of the sampling clock are effectively suppressed below the intrinsic thermal and quantization noise of the ADC.

articleTitle: Extraction of Audio Information from EM Emission Caused by Loose Connectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: When an electronic device is positioned near a speaker, speech information can be captured in unintentional electromagnetic (EM) emissions radiating from the device. This enables for the non-invasive retrieval of speech information from several meters without line-of-sight. Especially in this study, we explore a fundamental investigation into the feasibility of extracting audio information from EM emanations associated with “connectors with loosening.” This is because a loose connector has an “unstable physical structure” at its internal contact boundary and is susceptible to vibrations induced by the sound from the speaker. Specifically, we aim to restore audio information by measuring the common-mode currents generated by “connectors with loosening” positioned near the speaker. Our experiments demonstrate that audio information can be retrieved by applying both amplitude and phase demodulation techniques to the measured common-mode currents when the torque value of the sub-miniature type A (SMA) connectors used in the experiment is set to less than 2.00 cNm.

articleTitle: Predicting Electromagnetic Sensitivity in Multi-Waveform L-DACS1 Receivers through Spectral Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: L-band digital aeronautical communication system type 1 (L-DACS1) plays a vital role in digital aeronautical communication equipment, but its communication performance can be hampered by interference from other devices in the same frequency band and the natural electromagnetic environment. Predicting the electromagnetic sensitivity of L-DACS1 receivers is crucial for swiftly switching communication systems in response to external interference, ensuring uninterrupted communication.In this paper, we propose an electromagnetic sensitivity prediction method based on spectral feature extraction. We also create a communication simulation model to compare L-DACS1 with FMBC, spread spectrum FBMC (SSFBMC), and traditional OFDM. The results demonstrate the accuracy of our prediction method in estimating bit errors under various interference levels. Moreover, it confirms that using modulation with faster out-of-band fading and spread spectrum coding positively impacts the electromagnetic susceptibility of L-DACS1 receivers. This predictive method aids in identifying and mitigating electromagnetic interference, providing valuable guidance.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Testing the Electromagnetic Immunity of the Short Circuit Protection Function of Smart Power Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper investigates the robustness of the shortcircuit protection function of automotive smart power switches. These devices are being used more and more in vehicles and are performing more and more safety-related functions. Since a modern car is full of electronics, compliance with the relevant electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) standards is a prerequisite for safe operation. However, the EMC standards do not cover safety functions such as overtemperature or short-circuit protection. This can lead to a potential safety risk in the end product. Therefore, we present a system that combines the short circuit test and the direct power injection (DPI) immunity test to investigate the electromagnetic immunity of the short circuit protection function. We show a new test method, apply it on two representative devices from different manufacturers, and discuss the results. The short-circuit protection function of the tested devices seems to be robust against electromagnetic disturbances, while some weaknesses in the diagnostic output were found, which may lead to a misinterpretation of the failure state of the device under test (DUT).

articleTitle: An Algorithm to Find Interval Solution Ranges and Its Use to Improve Prediction Accuracy in Multi-Objective Optimal Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In the design process of electrical products, it is often necessary to find solutions that simultaneously satisfy multi-objective performance requirements that sometimes conflict. Such solutions are expected to be redundant to cover a wider range of design parameters. In this paper, we propose a new algorithm to find the interval solution ranges and calculate the range size. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm was used to find the interval solution ranges from the spectrum prediction through ANN-based machine learning algorithm for EMI filters used for noise suppression in brush motor drive systems. The relationship between recall and the magnitude of the interval solution range based on the confusion matrix indicates that lower recall does not result in a wider interval solution range. This suggests that reducing the number of false negatives (FN) and increasing the number of true positives (TP) will result in a better interval solution range.

articleTitle: Modeling of Common-Mode Noise Equivalent Circuit for Solid-State Transformer based on ISOP Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper discusses common-mode noise of a solid-state transformer (SST) based on input-series output-parallel (ISOP) configuration. The ISOP configuration has a complex common-mode current path because of the increased parasitic component of the switching devices. The power factor correction (PFC) part in the SST is modeled with a common-mode equivalent circuit in order to measure the characteristics of the common-mode current. The leakage current between the simulation and the experimental result is compared in order to evaluate the common-mode equivalent model. The maximum spectrum values of the leakage current in the simulation and the experimental result are $67.2 \mathrm{~dB} \mu \mathrm{A}$ and $63.6 \mathrm{~dB} \mu \mathrm{A}$ at the 4.5 MHz band. This means that the frequency 4.5MHz is the resonant frequency between the parasitic capacitor and the parasitic inductor of the switching devices. The experimental results of the leakage current envelope curve almost agree with the simulation results. Thus, the proposed common equivalent model is valid in order to evaluate the common mode current based on CISPR 16.

articleTitle: EMC Modeling of a Class-D Amplifier IC and Radiated Emission Correlation Studies for its Evaluation Board
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper presents the Radiated Emission (RE) correlation studies between the Electromagnetic Interference and Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMI/EMC) simulations and the corresponding chamber measurements for a Class-D amplifier IC. The primary aim of this paper is to analyze a device’s EMI/EMC performance and devise strategies to mitigate electromagnetic noise early in the design phase by simulations. Towards that objective, models are also developed to represent the noise behavior of Class-D amplifier IC, and the same are used in RE simulations to establish correlation with the measured data. Several iterative studies are presented to showcase the usefulness of simulations in predicting the failure region, early in the design phase for a Class D amplifier IC evaluation board with a switching frequency of 2 MHz.
