articleTitle: Development of Malfunction Simulation Technology in Electrostatic Discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: If ESD test fails, ESD countermeasures are often analyzed based on the actual equipment, so the analysis time and redesign increase. Recently, there has been a movement to utilize simulations in the upstream phase of development and countermeasures against malfunction. But there is no quantitative model for malfunction judgment, it is only risk extraction. This time, in order to quantify the judgment of ESD malfunction, we used TLP to reproduce the causes of malfunction in ESD tests, referring to the method standardized by IEC62433-6 and we confirmed its effectiveness.

articleTitle: In-Situ Investigation of Antenna Behavior in Close Proximity to Objects: A Practical Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In-situ measurements, especially in busy environment like hospitals, poses a range of challenges. Finding the best place for receiving antennas in such environments is often impractical or even impossible, leading to significant measurement errors. This paper focuses on assessing antenna performance near other structures encountered in typical onsite measurement scenarios to gauge the increase of the measurement uncertainty in the designated environment. Changes in the reflection coefficient values at the receiver antenna port serve as performance indicators. Measurements were performed for a telescopic dipole and a wideband discone antenna, conducted in close proximity to metallic and concrete walls, as well as an absorber surface, for various distances. The study concludes by discussing the anticipated measurement error levels observed in the measurements.

articleTitle: Effects of Air as Transmission Medium on Wave Propagation and Possibility of Generalization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper presents an experiment comparing specific frequencies and atmospheric variables to investigate possible relations. The secondary result is the probability function of the strength of the signal at that frequency. The proposed experiment is a stepping stone for further development in using probability functions in computational tasks such as simulations that would otherwise rely on ideal values. Increased computational power cannot solve this considerable inconsistency between reality and simulation. The signal was recorded using an FM radio tower near the measurement site, which allowed for tracking stable and strong electromagnetic radiation over a long period and occasional measurement near the transmitter. Atmospheric variables, such as air pollutants and humidity, were tracked to cross-compare them during the analysis. Conclusions were drawn based on several procedural analyses, which consisted of the time domain of the observed signal, probability function of signal strength, and cross-comparison time domains of signal and atmospheric variables.

articleTitle: Analysis of Conducted and Radiated Emission on a Self-oscillating Capacitive Touch Sensing Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: With the advent of smartphones, there has been a recent increase in the use of capacitive touch sensing for various Human Machine Interfaces (HMI). Capacitive-based touch sensing provides higher flexibility and cost-effectiveness than, methodologies such as resistive-based touch sensing. However, Capacitive-based touch sensing is more prone to disturbances such as Electromagnetic interference (EMI) and noise due to temperature variation. This effect becomes more dominating as the sensing excitation frequency increases. Traditional capacitance to digital circuits, such as sigma-delta capacitive sensing, requires multiple clock cycles to measure sensing capacitance, thus necessitating higher frequency operation. In turn, this produces challenges in Electromagnetic Emission while also increasing its susceptibility to EMI, such as false or ghost touch due to exposure of the sensing electrodes to various frequency electric fields. This paper discusses the conducted electromagnetic emission behavior of an external excitation-frequency independent self-oscillating capacitance-to-time converter, where sensing is done with a single clock cycle, and discusses radiated Electromagnetic emission of the touch sensing electrode. The proposed approach is suitable for touch-sensing applications, mainly when used in a noisy EMI environment, such as inside a vehicle within the Automotive industry.

articleTitle: Quad-Port MIMO Antenna Design with Low SAR for 3.5 GHz 5G and 5.8 GHz ISM Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: A 4-port MIMO antenna with a low specific absorption rate (SAR) is presented in this paper for $3.5 \mathrm{GHz} 5 \mathrm{G}$, and 5.8 GHz ISM (Industrial, Scientific, and Medical) band applications. The antenna is developed on a $0.252 \mathrm{~mm}$ thick Rogers 5880 substrate with a compact size of $36.2 \mathrm{~mm} \times 36.2$ mm. The designed antenna offers a bandwidth of more than 100 $\mathrm{MHz}(3.47-3.58 \mathrm{GHz}$), and $350 \mathrm{MHz}(5.64-6.01 \mathrm{GHz})$ at 3.5 GHz and 5.8GHz bands, respectively. The antenna also provides a good radiation efficiency higher than $90 \%$ within the functioning frequency bands with a peak gain of 2.01 dBi and 1.71 dBi at 3.5GHz and 5.8GHz, respectively. To check the radiation effect of the antenna in terms of SAR on the human tissue, a 3-layer biological tissue model is created. And, the SAR value of the designed antenna is calculated. With $125 \mathrm{~mW}$ of supply power, the proposed antenna shows a SAR value of 1.92 $\mathrm{W} / \mathrm{Kg}$ and $0.465 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{kg}$ averaging on $10 \mathrm{~g}$ of tissue, while the antenna is positioned $10 \mathrm{~mm}$ away from the 3-layer human tissue model. The suggested antenna is a good fit for dual-band MIMO systems operating at sub-6 GHz based on its overall performance metrics.

articleTitle: Multiple Transient Voltage Suppressor Diodes-Based Protection Circuits with Decreasing Loading Effect Under High-Power Microwave Pulses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This study demonstrates multiple transient voltage suppressor (TVS) diodes-based protection circuits under high-power microwave (HPM) pulses to protect sensitive semiconductor and microwave devices from interference or even damaged by intentionally electromagnetic interference (IEMI). Firstly, the nonlinear large signal model of two adopted types of TVS diodes are studied. Secondly, a transmission line (TL) is applied to compensate degrade of RF performance resulted from TVS diode capacitance. Therefore, protection circuits based on multiple TVS diodes are proposed and measured under HPM pulses with their overshoot protection ratio (PR) recorded. The highest overshoot protection ratio (PR) of-these circuits is approximately 17-20dB when the input HPM pulse power ranges from 50 to 63 dBm. Measured results are correlated with simulated results.

articleTitle: A Universal Interference-Simulator for Digitally Modulated Communication Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This contribution describes the development of a universal simulation tool for assessing electromagnetic interferences of nowadays broadband digitally modulated communication standards. It discusses the applicability of current emission test procedures with resolution bandwidths much higher than the typical subcarrier spacing of digital standards, where unlike for analogue modulated signals the information is distributed in a broadband spectrum. The simulation comprises a generalized structure to be applicable to all kind of digitally modulated standards, even future ones. First simulation results are presented for the nowadays mobile communication standards. A major advantage of the presented simulation tool is, that it relates the properties of interferences signals, i.e., bandwidth and amplitude, to an error probability of individual standard’s functions, for example a decrease in data rate. This allows a much more sophisticated assessment of interferers, than just limit values of interferers, which are exceeded or not, associated with a system to operate or not.

articleTitle: Detection Sensitivity Improvement in Sequence Time Domain Reflectometry by Removing Pulse Reflected at Nodes in Bus Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Since the sequence time domain reflection can reduce the influence of background noise by cross-correlating the transmitted and reflected pulses, our motivation lies in its use for anomaly detection in bus networks. The problems here are that not only is the pulse amplitude reduced when traveling over a node in a bus network, but also the reflected pulse modulated by M-sequence from the node causes a reduction in detection sensitivity. Therefore, by making the pulse cross-correlated with the transmitted pulse not just a reflected pulse but the difference between the reflected pulses during normal and anomaly statuses, the effect of reflected pulses generated at the nodes can be removed and the sensitivity of anomaly detection can be improved. When a 20 pF capacitive anomaly exists on a line with a characteristic impedance of 120 $\Omega$, applying the method with a series length K=63 and a symbol length $T_{\mathrm{c}}$=10 ns of sinusoidal pulses, the anomaly detection sensitivity after the second node improved from 0.10 to 0.53 without background noise. Furthermore, it was found that the anomaly detection sensitivity could be improved even in the presence of additive white Gaussian noise.

articleTitle: Study on Design of Bend Differential-Paired Lines With Low Common-Mode Noise Using Topology Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Common-mode (CM) noise is generated and radiated in bend differential-paired lines due to imbalance components resulting from the difference in length between the two signal lines. CM components are often compensated for such as by equal-length routing, but equal-length routing requires a large area, which hinders miniaturization. Aiming to design bend differential-paired lines with low CM noise by thinking outside the box, topology optimization is used, in which a structural optimization method with a high degree of freedom, is applied to the bending section in this paper. A Normalized Gaussian Network (NGnet) is used to represent the structure to enable a smooth representation, and the micro genetic algorithm $(\mu \mathrm{GA})$ is used as an optimization algorithm to search for solutions globally through the evaluation of a small number of individuals. In addition, it is examined how optimization results are affected by narrowing down the design target and by increasing the expressive power by changing the number of bases of NGnet. As a result of optimization, a structure with better performance is designed by narrowing down the design target to only the inner line and by increasing the number of cells in the design area. Furthermore, a design that has a high degree of freedom is possible by generating the initial structure randomly, indicating the possibility of better designs for differential-paired lines.

articleTitle: Design of high voltage ripple immunity test protection based on coupling mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The safety of new energy vehicles remains an important issue. Through analyzing the safety accidents of new energy vehicles, it is found that these accidents have complex and systematic characteristics, among which the ripple in the high-voltage system is one of the main factors affecting safety. At present, high-voltage ripple testing standards have been gradually introduced, but the testing details and protection methods for high-voltage ripple immunity are not yet being perfected. Therefore, the paper focuses on the immunity testing of high-voltage ripple, analyzes the electrical characteristics of key components of new energy vehicles, and conducts systematic protection design. These designs include voltage balancing and stabilizing systems, optimizing system voltage losses, strengthening fault monitoring and protection mechanisms, and enhancing electrical isolation and insulation performance. By comprehensively applying these strategies, the safety and reliability of high-voltage ripple immunity testing can be improved, which has positive significance for the development of high-voltage testing standards.

articleTitle: Statistical Modeling of Automotive Component Noise-Source in accordance with the Load Change
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electromagnetic noise is often a phenomenon with large fluctuation, therefore, it is useful to understand the noise source characteristics including fluctuations in order to design the emissions from a system. For this reason, a method is proposed to construct a statistical model by applying a generalized extreme value distribution to each frequency of noise current obtained by repeatedly measuring on a bench. It aims at obtaining a practical model by a simple method, not a rigid model construction. The method is applied to the noise current from an in-vehicle DCDC converter, and the estimation accuracy of the statistical distribution has been verified. As a result, it is shown that the distribution and the upper limit of noise intensity can be estimated with practical accuracy below 700MHz.

articleTitle: Improvement of Functional Printed Patterns for Electrical Over Stress Protection and its Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electrical overstress (EOS) protection is necessary for electric equipment to prevent malfunctions and failures caused by high voltage applications due to electrostatic discharge (ESD) or lightning surge. Previous research proposed a functional printed pattern for EOS protection. The pattern was diamond-shaped conductors placed between the lines on a printed circuit board. When the EOS is applied, the pattern makes a gap between the lines conductive by ESDs. In this study, we improve the shape of the elements of the functional printed pattern to lower the operating voltage and improve the stability of the protection operation. As a result, the proposed pattern with a reduced area of the elements achieved the operation voltage of $1.3 \mathrm{kV}, 200 \mathrm{~V}$ lower than the previous pattern. In addition, the proposed pattern can operate more stable than the previous pattern. Furthermore, it was confirmed that the insertion loss of the proposed pattern measured using a $50 \Omega$ matched CPWG measuring board was small, less than approximately $0.6 \mathrm{~dB}$ at frequency ranges from 100kHz to 1GHz.

articleTitle: Development of Emulator Simulating Transmission of Undersea Radio Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The authors’ research group is engaged in research and development of undersea radio communication technology. To improve communication efficiency, antenna characteristic and communication system are being developed through actual measurement. However, it is not easy to conduct large-scale measurement because of the time and cost required for preparation. Therefore, an undersea communication emulator that simulates undersea radio wave attenuation is being built to simplify large-scale experiment. In this paper, an undersea communication emulator of the transmission characteristic obtained by actual measurement is fabricated, and comparison of transmission characteristic and communication performance are shown through communication experiment. As a result of evaluating the communication characteristics of the fabricated emulator, it was confirmed that the transmission characteristic was expressed with a difference of less than 1 dB in a bandwidth of approximately 85 % of the carrier frequency, and that the transmission rate could be simulated with an accuracy of less than 1 Mbps.

articleTitle: Design of a Wi-Fi-Compatible Common-Mode Noise Filter Using Dual-Band Matching Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Modern digital signal transmission heavily relies on differential-mode signals. However, challenges such as asymmetrical routing, bending, and timing skew can compromise their symmetry, leading to common-mode noise issues. To address this challenge, we propose a dual-band absorptive common-mode noise suppression filter incorporating a series unified dual-band matching network. This approach effectively maintains the integrity of differential signals while suppressing common-mode noise. The proposed architecture has been verified to achieve an absorption efficiency of over 80% in the target frequency bands of 2.4-2.48 GHz and 5.18-5.32 GHz. They are furthermore, adding the dual-band matching network results in only a slight increase in the overall footprint. This implementation presents a promising solution for mitigating electromagnetic interference (EMI) challenges in digital signal transmission.

articleTitle: A Universal Software Defined Radio Setup for Measuring Airport NavCom Infractures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This contribution discusses the feasibility of performing inspection and compliance measurements of airport navigation and surveillance infrastructures by means of commercially available software defined radios. With the advanced technology in the field of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) inspection measurements could be conducted with drones, which allow a very effective way for assessing a large space around airport infrastructures. Since basically in-situ measurements of such navigation systems require always at least two channels, i.e. one channel for measuring the signal variation in space, and one channel for calibration of statistical effects of the system, a multi-channel software defined radio (SDR) setup provides a commercially available solution for this type of measurements. A universal setup of such a system is discussed in this contribution, along with a performance assessment of uncertainties in a laboratory setup. Finally, example measurements are presented for a UAV-flight inspection of an instrument landing system at an airport.

articleTitle: Experimental study results of EMC 5G network transmitters and fixed service receivers for sharing utilization of 4.4-5.0 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: According to the GSA database, dozens of countries around the world have utilized or are planning to use the n79 band (4.4 - 5.0 GHz), which is defined by 3GPP as the 5G band. At WRC-19, over 40 countries identified some or all of the spectrum in this band for IMT-2020/5G. This band, as per the Radio Regulations and the ECA, is also allocated to microwave links (MWL) of the Fixed service. The sharing of the n79 band (4.4 - 5.0 GHz) between 5G networks and MWL may cause harmful interference to fixed service radio receivers. This article presents the results of an experimental study on the protection criteria for typical MWLs in case of interferences from transmitters of 5G networks using the 4.4-5.0 GHz band. The obtained results allow for solving the EMC problem for its shared utilization.

articleTitle: Analysis of mode conversion using modal equivalent circuits for immunity evaluation of high-speed communication equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this report, the mechanism of mode conversion of interfering electromagnetic waves injected into communication equipment from coaxial cables to in-vehicle communication modules is evaluated and clarified from the viewpoint of immunity. A mode conversion equivalent circuit was used for this purpose. Considering radiated immunity, the applied electromagnetic field induces a common-mode current in the coaxial cable, which propagates through the cable to the signal line inside the enclosure via a connector. When microstrip lines are used within a printed circuit board, the imbalance difference between the two transmission lines causes a conversion from common-mode current to normal-mode voltage. Furthermore, when the imbalance difference is small, the parasitic inductance between the ground connections at the connectors is dominant in the mode conversion. To evaluate these phenomena, a mode transformation circuit with ideal transformers was created. The circuit simulations were conducted using the model and a modal transmission line. The obtained results showed the same trend as that of the 3D electromagnetic field simulation.

articleTitle: Study on Crosstalk and Mode Conversion of Two Pairs of Differential-Paired Lines with Different Distances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: It is desired that EMC guidelines and ways of designing multi-conductor differential-paired lines at high frequency be established on the basis of research work on fundamental knowledge. To provide basic considerations for crosstalk and mode conversion of two pairs of differential-paired lines with different distances, this paper studies the dependencies of crosstalk and mode conversion evaluated with a mixed-mode S-parameter on the distance between two differential-paired lines using theoretical calculation and FDTD modeling. Good agreement between theoretical calculations and results calculated by FDTD demonstrates the validity of the proposed theoretical calculations. The dependencies of crosstalk and mode conversion are quantified. The proposed method provides enough flexibility for different geometric parameters and can be used to gain physical insights and develop design guidelines. This study has successfully established a basic method for effectively predicting crosstalk and mode conversion on two pairs of differential-paired lines.

articleTitle: Radiated Emissions of a Shielded Cable Excited by a Differential Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: The cables attached to a power converter are typically the main antennas for radiated emissions. The relevant current that leads to radiation is the total current on the cable, which is therefore called antenna mode current. A key part of EMC analysis is the understanding of the mechanism driving these antenna mode currents, in order to find proper shielding or filtering mechanism to reduce these currents. The imbalance difference theory allows to quantitatively describe the creation of antenna mode currents and is applied here to a setup consisting of a shielded cable with pigtails for different loads. Normal modes described by transmission line theory are converted to antenna modes causing radiation from the cable. Measurements, theoretical analysis, and full wave simulations of radiation are presented and are all in good agreement.

articleTitle: Communication Speed Estimation of Undersea Wavelet-OFDM Communication under EM Noise Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: As the marine business expands, there is a growing demand for real-time capturing of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) status using radio frequency communications. On the other hand, electromagnetic noise emitted by AUVs can interfere with communications. To investigate the impact of electromagnetic noise in undersea Wavelet-OFDM communication, the author constructed an experimental setup that simulates the radio wave transmission characteristics of underwater antennas without the experimental environment in the sea and introduced external noise to assess communication speed. The authors compared the noise power induced in the receiver to the communication speed using the proposed evaluation setup. The results shows that when the distance between the loop antennas was 1 m, communication was disabled by applying a -90 dBm disturbance. Additionally, the author proposed a method to estimate communication speed using transmission characteristics and measured electromagnetic noise. The communication speeds calculated using the proposed method agreed with the measured results with a maximum error of 1.65 Mbps. Improving accuracy remains a challenge for future research.

articleTitle: A Novel Reconfigurable Metasurface with Expanded Tuning Range for Electromagnetic Interference Shielding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel reconfigurable metasurface with an expanded tuning range, which addresses the limitations of conventional band-stop structures. A unique method that utilizes varactor diodes for continuous tunability in single polarization and PIN diodes for mode switching capabilities are proposed, and newly designed structures are provided and validated through full-wave simulations. The innovative design significantly extends the frequency tuning range from 2.24 - 3.67 GHz to 2.15 - 5.46 GHz, demonstrating enhanced broadband performance suitable for modern intelligent antenna systems. This advanced metasurface has the potential to meet the evolving demands for dynamic electromagnetic compatibility in various communication applications.

articleTitle: Partial Image Expansion Applied to Real Near-Field Measurement Data Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This work uses the partial image expansion method to build an infinitesimal dipole model (IDM) of a physical Printed Circuit Board (PCB) starting from the measured near-fields. Using partial image expansion allows to include the substrate directly in the equivalent model, that is composed of PEC plane, substrate and dipole sources. The addition of the dielectric increases the model versatility allowing for a wider range of simulations to be run (e.g. closed environments, multiple boards, etc.). In this paper, the radiation model of the physical device is obtained and imported in a commercial full-wave solver (HFSS). The simulation results are finally compared with the original measurements, experimentally validating the accuracy of an IDM built using partial image expansion.

articleTitle: Immunity test result and consideration of open-source flight-controller mounting UAV for applying IEMI protection device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Recently, UAVs are used for a variety of services such as agriculture, aerial photography, inspection, and logistics, and are also used for weather observation. NTT R&D is conducting research on how to prevent damage to equipment and people from lightning by flying UAVs equipped with lightning protection capabilities at high altitudes near thunderclouds and receiving lightning strikes. To develop a lightning-resistant UAV, it is first necessary to consider the UAV immunity and vulnerability. UAV flight controllers are equipped with many sensors, and failure of the sensor itself, inability to control attitude due to sensor signal communication errors, stoppage due to power regulator failure, thermal damage to motor drivers, rare short in the diode. A crush accident may be caused by these failures. Therefore, it is necessary to take countermeasures at vulnerable points. However, although CISPR and other organizations are working to develop international standards for immunity testing methods to UAV, they have not yet been established now. For this reason, we will introduce our own immunity testing method for UAV equipped with open-source flight-controller and the results.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Numerical Simulation Study on the Synergistic Effects of Transient Ionizing Radiation and Electromagnetic Pulse on Bipolar Junction Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Utilizing semiconductor device simulation tools, a study was conducted on the transient current response of bipolar junction transistors under the synergistic effects of transient ionizing radiation and electromagnetic pulses. The results indicate that, under positive forward bias conditions, the synergistic effect of positive polarity pulse injected into the base and transient ionizing radiation exceeds the linear superposition of their individual effects. However, with an increase in the amplitude of the electromagnetic pulses, the synergistic effect gradually converges towards the outcome observed when electromagnetic pulses act in isolation. Furthermore, the synergistic effect of positive polarity pulse injected into the collector and transient ionizing radiation surpasses the linear superposition of their individual effects. Notably, as the amplitude of the electromagnetic pulses increases, the synergistic effect deviates increasingly from the linear superposition of their individual effects.

articleTitle: Study on Influence of Leakage Flux Dependence on Winding Position of Common-mode Choke Coil Using Toroidal Core
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: An equivalent circuit model of the coils is required to study the performance of the choke. This model must represent both the normal and common modes and the electromagnetic couplings between the windings. In this research, the leakage flux dependence on the winding position were evaluated by using a single-phase common-mode choke coil of nanocrystalline alloy and Mn-Zn cores. As a result, the leakage inductance increased up to twice independent of the frequency with opposing wind-ings position. It was also found from the simulation that the change in leakage inductance is due to the change in leakage flux, which is determined by the size of the core.

articleTitle: Improved Neural Network-based High-frequency Behavioral Modeling of Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: High-frequency (HF) modeling of induction motors plays a key role in predicting motor terminal overvoltage and conducted emissions in a motor drive system. In this paper, a neural network based HF modeling method is proposed, which has the merits of high accuracy and good versatility. The proposed model of the induction motor consists of a three-phase equivalent circuit, which can be expanded by an increment of 7 elements per phase to ensure model accuracy. The motor physics knowledge, namely per phase impedances, are used in the artificial neural network to obtain the values of the circuit elements. The parameterization can be easily implemented using a common personal computer (PC). The case studies verify the effectiveness of the proposed HF modeling method.

articleTitle: An EMI Immune Daisy Chain Interface for Battery Management System Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Battery management systems (BMS) in electric vehicles (EVs) require robust communication interfaces for accurate monitoring and control of lithium-ion battery cells. This paper proposes an EMI-immune daisy chain interface circuit, utilizing either a capacitor or a transformer as an isolator. The system includes a transmitter an active receiver, and a wake-up receiver, achieving a successful transmission under 39-dBm EMI injection. Simulation results demonstrate a CMTI of 100kV/$\mu$ s and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Quantum Optimization of Microwave Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility problems may be extremely computationally expensive and the introduction of evolutionary optimization may need tens of thousands of fitness evaluations. The recent introduction of quantum computing may be extremely effective also in this research field to speed up the EMC compliant design process. In this paper, the problems and the potential of the introduction of quantum computing in evolutionary optimized microwave design has been investigated.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electrical Stress of Switched-Mode Power Supply (SMPS) on Conductive Electromagnetic Pulses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this paper, conductive stress analysis was conducted through electronic switched-mode power supply (SMPS) circuit modeling and experiments. When electronic devices are exposed to unintended electromagnetic pulses, problems may occur in the operation of SMPS. To protect devices from threatening problems such as conductive electromagnetic pulse (EMP), it is necessary to analyze damage mechanisms caused by electrical stress during electronic device operation. Therefore, in this paper, we manufactured a circuit board that simulates the SMPS of electronic devices and analyzed the effect on electric fast transient (EFT) through experiments and simulations. As a result of the analysis, the noise is mainly attenuated through the input filter, and the input rectifier diodes may break down after the filter burns out, resulting in a breakdown of the power supply. The results of this research can be used as preliminary research on evaluating the impact of SMPS on electronic devices caused by high-power electromagnetic waves such as EMP, surge, and intentional electromagnetic interference (IEMI).

articleTitle: Compliance Evaluations of Inductive WPT Systems with Basic Restrictions by Computational Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: In this study, we address the issue of how to evaluate with known uncertainty the fields of and exposure to inductive commercial wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. This work contributes to the development of the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standard IEC 63184 for testing the compliance of WPT systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Electromagnetic Shielding of Small Shield Bag for Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: This study proposes a method of determining the effectiveness of electromagnetic shielding. This method is advantageous because it can be used to test small shield bags using battery-powered comb generators. The proposed method is then applied to a letter-size shield bag developed for use in aircraft cabins.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetic Interference Compensation Method for Dense Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Joint International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility, Signal & Power Integrity: EMC Japan / Asia-Pacific International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC Japan/APEMC Okinawa)
abstract: Dense antenna arrays have the potential to increase the effective channel number of a multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) system, which could cope with the high demands for data rates in future communication systems. However, the strong coupling effect caused by the tight antenna elements will deteriorate the desired transmitting beams, and then cause severe electromagnetic interference (EMI) problems. To address this problem, this paper proposes a beam coupling compensation method for dense antenna arrays. Specifically, the mutual coupling effect is described as the modal excitation coefficients between different antenna elements. Combined with the beam synthesis results based on the array factor (AF), the actual excitation of each antenna element is modified to achieve the desired beampattern, which is significant to solve the EMI problems. This proposed method can handle the beam synthesis problems for dense antenna arrays without any decoupling devices with high isolation. Finally, some numerical cases are presented to validate the proposed method.
